# Development Log

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 3: annotated-figure overlay recreation

Implemented Phase 3 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan on `feat/presentify-visual-fidelity` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal gate). When a source figure is a base image carrying author-added annotations (map regions, colored zones, callout labels, leader lines), those annotations are now recreated as a registered interactive overlay on the extracted base image, instead of being demoted to a textual list beside a flat map. **3.1 protocol (reference)**: `references/figure-reconstruction.md` part 1 records an `annotated: true` signal alongside the base `classification`, and part 5 is rewritten from a binary (full SVG rebuild OR flat enhanced-original) into a THREE-way decision that adds the OVERLAY-RECREATION path: keep the base image at native resolution; recreate each annotation in a registered overlay layer normalized to the base image with PERCENTAGE coords (so it scales); make it interactive (hover/focus highlight, click-toggle legend, keyboard focus, a lightbox that moves base + overlay together); and carry the provenance badge + view-original toggle. The side-text list is kept as an ACCESSIBLE COMPLEMENT, never the replacement (the exact defect being fixed). **3.2 gate + accounting (reference)**: part 4 gates overlays on confidence (high/medium recreate; low ships the enhanced original + textual complement with NO fabricated regions), part 6 adds the overlay to the model round-trip, and the coverage-reconciliation output format gains an `[overlay-reconstructed]` line plus the resolution-list update. **3.3 extractor**: `scripts/extract_content.py` now captures PPTX overlay shapes drawn over a picture as an `annotations` array on that image block. `_iter_pptx_shapes` was extended to carry the enclosing group name, and the `_extract_pptx` inner loop became a two-pass walk: pass 1 finds picture placed-rectangles; pass 2 assigns any non-picture shape whose CENTER lies inside a picture AND whose area is smaller than it as an annotation (image-relative bbox, text, solid fill/line hex colors best-effort, group name) and CONSUMES it so it is not also emitted as a stray text block; pass 3 builds blocks in document order and attaches the annotations to the image block. A shape beside (not over) a picture stays normal content. `content-model.md` documents the new `annotations` field (image-relative bbox rationale) and `extraction-runbook.md` documents the PPTX capture + the flattened-PDF agent-vision path. **Extractor regression proof**: the committed extractor and the new extractor BOTH score 41 PASS / 4 FAIL on `verify_phase1.py`, where the 4 FAILs are environmental (no `rapidocr-onnxruntime` locally, so scanned-page OCR degrades) and all 8 PPTX checks pass - so the two-pass restructure changed nothing for the existing fixtures. **3.4 builder + tests**: the deterministic baseline builder was extended to recreate the overlay from the `annotations` metadata (`build_presentation.py` `_render_annotated_figure` + `assets/presentation-template.html` overlay CSS), because it is the only deterministic producer of "authored HTML" the phase's end-to-end test can assert against. It renders a `.fig-annotated` figure: the base image, a `.fig-overlay` layer of percentage-positioned `.fig-region` elements (each with its label, fill via a `--region-color` custom property, `tabindex` + `role`/`aria-label`), a `.fig-legend`, a provenance badge, and a CSS-ONLY view-original toggle (a hashed-id checkbox + `<label for>` driving `.fig-toggle:checked ~ .fig-figure .fig-overlay { display: none }`, no JS). Offline (the self-check passes; hex colors and percentage coords trip no fetch guard). `tests/skills/test_presentify_annotations.py` (5 cases): the extractor captures the two over-map shapes as annotations (0..1 bbox, labels, fill) and leaves the sidebar text as a paragraph; the end-to-end annotated-map PPTX -> extractor -> builder -> HTML contains a registered overlay (one `.fig-region` per source region, the labels, a legend, a view-original toggle); the dependency-free builder test asserts the region percentage coords + provenance + offline; the no-annotations fixture emits NO fabricated regions (the low-confidence/flattened degrade); and a headless-optional toggle test skips-with-note without a browser. **CI**: no edit needed - `presentify-extractor.yml` already runs the whole `tests/skills/` dir under a `tests/skills/**` path filter (Phase 2), so the new test file is covered; concurrency + pip cache present; no headless job. **Gates**: ruff clean on the extractor + builder + test; orphan audit 0 errors; unicode 0 errors; full `tests/skills` suite 40 pass / 3 skip (the 3 skips are the headless-render checks). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is authoritative. **Scope note**: the builder-overlay rendering (`3.4a`) is not one of the plan's named sub-tasks (which are reference + extractor + tests), but the plan's 3.4 acceptance ("assert the authored HTML contains a registered overlay layer") requires a deterministic HTML producer, so the builder consuming the extractor's `annotations` is the in-spirit realization that makes Phase 3 end-to-end testable. **Known gaps**: DF-3 added (the overlay-detection heuristic - center-inside plus smaller-than-picture - would capture full-slide-background body text; the LLM-native path applies judgment; documented in the runbook gotchas). DF-1/DF-2 and BG-1 carry from Phases 1-2, untouched. Phases 4-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 2: image sizing and placement discipline

Implemented Phase 2 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan on `feat/presentify-visual-fidelity` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal gate). Gave every extracted image a prominence-appropriate, bounded box with no meaningful-content crop and no dead space at 100% zoom, and named the inverse-of-contact-sheet failure (a secondary image ballooned to hero scale) as a defect. Command + skill + references + docs behavior only; no `base-*.md` lockstep, no installer edit, no new outbound call / dependency / credential. **2.1 measurable rules**: extended `references/interactive-features.md` "Prominence preservation" with four image-box rules, each carrying an observable metric the Phase 5 QA gate grades: a hero height cap (~80vh, so rendered-height/viewport-height stays <= ~0.8); a secondary cap that forbids a low-`page_fraction` image from being enlarged past its section's hero (the explicit inverse of the contact-sheet defect); an object-fit / crop policy (`object-fit: contain` plus a matched background for anything whose content `cover` would clip, `cover` reserved for decorative backdrops, with cropping a chart axis / labeled region / face called a defect and the metric being rendered-vs-native aspect ratio within ~2 percent); and a no-oversized-tile rule for galleries. Added a dead-space ceiling (~30% whitespace within an image band) to "Spacing and density". **2.2 extractor signals (CONFIRMED, no code change)**: verified `scripts/extract_content.py` already emits `page_fraction` and native `width`/`height` for image blocks on BOTH formats the rules depend on - PPTX picture shapes (`_pptx_image_block`, fraction = shape area / slide area) and PDF embedded rasters (fraction = bbox area / page area) - and that `references/content-model.md` already documents these v3 prominence fields; nothing was missing, so no extractor or schema edit was made and the new prominence test is the confirmation artifact. Empirically confirmed by building a python-pptx deck (`shape-picture page_fraction=0.142 width=400 height=267`) and a reportlab text+image PDF (`embedded-raster page_fraction=0.124 width=600 height=400`); a Pillow one-page image-only PDF is correctly classified `scanned-page` (no page geometry, so no `page_fraction`, by design). **2.3 template caps**: `assets/presentation-template.html` `figure img` now carries `max-height: 80vh` + `object-fit: contain` + a matched `background` (aspect preserved via `height: auto` + `max-width`, so no crop and no distortion), and a new token-driven `.gallery` grid caps each tile (a minimum tile width via `minmax` plus `max-height: 40vh` + `object-fit: contain`) so no secondary image balloons. Token-driven and offline (rebuild greps clean; self-check rc=0). **2.4 tests + CI**: added `tests/skills/test_presentify_extractor_prominence.py` (PPTX via python-pptx, PDF via reportlab, both `importorskip`-guarded so they run in the `presentify-extractor` workflow and skip in the deps-light `ci.yml` tests job) asserting populated `page_fraction` + native dimensions; extended `tests/skills/test_presentify_layout.py` with a browser-free image-cap assertion (max-height, object-fit, `.gallery`) and a headless-optional rendered image-box check (skip-with-note without a browser). Broadened `presentify-extractor.yml`'s path filter to `tests/skills/**` and pointed its pytest step at the whole `tests/skills/` dir (that runner installs the heavy extractor libs, so the prominence tests execute there; concurrency + pip cache already present). **Gates**: ruff clean on the builder + both test files; orphan audit 0 errors; unicode 0 errors; workflow-security pass; CI YAML parses; full `tests/skills` suite 36 pass / 2 skip (the 2 skips are the by-design headless-render checks; the extractor prominence tests actually ran and passed locally). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is the authoritative gate. **Known gaps**: two new documented, non-blocking deferrals - DF-1 (the baseline builder still stacks images and does not emit the new `.gallery` grouping or classify hero-vs-secondary from `page_fraction`; the gallery styles are latent for the LLM-native path, which is the primary target per the reference) and DF-2 (a PDF embedded raster's `page_fraction` is null when pdfplumber's per-page image-bbox count does not match the extracted raster count, the intentional geometry-alignment guard; native dimensions still rank, and PPTX + PDF rasterized-regions always carry the fraction). BG-1 (the Phase 1 builder color-var mismatch) remains open and untouched. Phases 3-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 1: full-width canvas contract

Implemented Phase 1 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal refactor gate). Made "full-width" a concrete, measurable edge-to-edge canvas across both the LLM-native authoring path and the deterministic baseline builder, with the body reading measure kept per-element. Command + skill + references + docs behavior only - no `base-*.md` five-platform lockstep, no installer edit (the bundle is folder-auto-copied), no new outbound call / dependency / credential. **1.1 reference contract**: replaced the prose "Full-width" bullet in `references/interactive-features.md` ("Output aspect (the canvas)") with an enforceable contract - page shell spanning the viewport via named `--gutter` tokens (not a centered `max-width` column); full-bleed top-level bands; the 45-85ch `--measure` scoped PER LONG-FORM-PROSE ELEMENT only (never the wrapper, headings, hero text, charts, tables, or image bands); and the success metric the verification and the Phase 5 gate use (at 1920px the widest top-level content band reaches at least ~95% of the viewport after gutters, with no global zoom / `transform: scale()`) - plus a one-line "failure to avoid" note (the narrow-centered-column-only-right-at-200%-zoom defect). Kept standard / portrait / other unchanged. **1.2 SKILL.md**: tightened Step 6's "Use the viewport width on purpose" and "Spacing, density, and aspect" bullets to cite the contract by name and state the binary full-width rule, and added a distinct Common Rationalizations row rebutting "the user chose full-width, but I'll keep one tidy centered column so it's safe" (a centered column with empty margins is a defect at full-width, not caution). SKILL.md stays well under the 800-line soft cap. **1.3 builder + template**: added `--layout {full|standard|portrait}` (default standard) to `build_presentation.py`; it injects a `--page-max`/`--gutter` pair into a new `NEXUS_ASPECT` marker block (mirroring the existing `NEXUS_THEME` mechanism, so no `[data-aspect]`-selector specificity conflict) and stamps `data-aspect` on the root `<html>`. `assets/presentation-template.html` now drives the canvas from those vars (`--slide-max` -> `--page-max`; `.slide` horizontal padding -> `--gutter`; `.slide__body` max-width -> `--page-max`), widens a full-width chart to its band, gates the >=1700px projector-padding widening to non-full aspects so full-width stays edge-to-edge, and keeps `--measure` scoped to prose. `full` = page-max 100% + small gutters (~96.7% band at 1920px); `standard` = the historical 1180px centered column (byte-identical to today's look); `portrait` = a 46rem reading column. **1.3 DEVIATION (root-cause fix)**: while verifying the builder I found a PRE-EXISTING bug - the title-substitution regex `<title>.*?</title>` (DOTALL) matched the header comment's literal "<title>" mention and spanned to the real `</title>`, deleting the comment close, `<html>`, `<head>`, and the `<meta>` tags on EVERY build (the baseline builder had been emitting headless, malformed HTML, unnoticed because no test checked builder output structure and `assert_no_external` strips comments first). Confirmed pre-existing by building from the committed template. Fixed the root cause (`<title>[^<]*</title>`, which cannot span across other tags) because Phase 1.3 requires a valid `<html data-aspect="...">` with an intact head; logged inline as a `# DEVIATION:`. **1.4 tests + CI**: `tests/skills/test_presentify_layout.py` (11 pass / 1 skip) asserts the injected `--page-max`/`--gutter`/`data-aspect` per layout, offline-cleanliness, head integrity (the TITLE_RE regression guard), and a browser-free CSS heuristic proving the >=95% full-width / <95% standard metric; it also ships the headless-optional `measure_widest_band` helper (the Phase 5 gate seed) whose true-render check skips-with-note when no browser is present. Broadened the `presentify-extractor.yml` path filter from `scripts/**` to the whole bundle + the new test, added `pytest`, and wired in the layout suite (concurrency cancel-in-progress + pip cache already present; no headless-render job added - that is gated to a later phase per the plan). **Gates**: ruff clean on the builder + test; `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` 0 errors; `validate_unicode_safety.py` 0 errors; `validate_workflow_security.py` pass; the CI YAML parses; full `tests/skills` suite 33 pass / 1 skip. `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is the authoritative full-suite gate. **Known gaps**: BG-1 (a PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope builder color-var mismatch - `theme_to_css` emits `--color-background`/`--color-foreground` while the template consumes `--color-bg`/`--color-fg`, so built output loses theme colors; recorded, not fixed, per scope discipline) and MT-1 (the rendered-width check skips without a headless browser; the metric is covered browser-free by the CSS heuristic, and a gated headless-render job is deferred to Phase 5). Phases 2-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.3 adoption-no-ai-slop Phase 1: author the anti-slop-editing skill and bundle

Implemented Phase 1 of the no-ai-slop adoption plan on `develop` - a new `anti-slop-editing` skill that removes named AI-slop prose patterns while preserving the writer's voice, and can detect slop without rewriting. Every candidate in this plan is `skill-native` (MCP Registry Policy tier 2: pure LLM instructions, zero new code / outbound call / dependency / credential), so the whole phase is authoring four files under `catalog/skills/developer-experience/anti-slop-editing/`. **1.1 SKILL.md**: quoted single-line `description` (241 chars, under the 250 ceiling), `summary_l0` (13 words), `overview_l1` (~120 words), and the required body sections in order - title + intro, When to Use (with an explicit When-NOT-to-use pointing generic writing to `writing-editing` and UI slop to `hallmark-design`), a Two-Modes table (Edit default / Detect), Instructions, a 17-entry named-pattern catalog (binary contrasts, throat-clearing openers, faux-insight setups, colon reveals, superficial -ing analysis, importance puffery, weasel attribution, fake-strong verbs, synonym cycling, negative listing, dramatic fragmentation, robotic rhythm, rhetorical setups, fake-profound kickers, summary-recap endings, formatting slop, and em-dash discipline) each with a quoted smell + a concrete before/after fix, Voice-Preservation Discipline, a wired Self-Check Loop, Common Rationalizations, a binary Verification checklist, and Related Skills cross-links (`[[writing-editing]]`, `[[hallmark-design]]`, `[[technical-writer]]`, `[[strategic-comments]]`). The em-dash guidance adopts the project ceiling (no em-dashes AND no clause-joining spaced hyphens), stronger than the source's "one or two are fine". Per the reverse-engineering attribution rule, no external repo/product/author/course is named anywhere in the bundle. **1.2 references/slop-wordlist.md**: banned words, often-empty adverbs, and empty phrases, each framed as judgment guidance (cut when empty, keep when it carries emphasis/contrast/uncertainty/voice) with keep-it/cut-it examples, cross-linked to the project Communication Style rules. **1.3 references/self-check.md + wiring**: a pass/fail content-quality rubric (point + voice preserved, proportional cutting, ASCII punctuation, mode-specific checks) that the SKILL.md Workflow grades its own output against and loops fix-and-recheck until clean, all in one agent; the SKILL.md body distinguishes this runtime self-check from the artifact-level Verification section and the routing-level trigger-cases. **1.4 evals/trigger-cases.json**: 4 positives + 4 near-miss negatives (v3.15.2 schema). The `description` and the eval prompts were lexically co-engineered against the deterministic router: every positive's surviving tokens (slop / read / detect / pattern / remove / robotic / filler / keep / writer / voice) live in the description so it scores ~1.0 and outranks `hallmark-design` (shares only "slop") and `writing-editing` (shares none of them), while the negatives deliberately avoid the description's vocabulary so the strongest near-miss stays near zero and the 1.15x margin clears. **1.5 validation**: `validate_skills.py` on the skill PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings - quoted description parses under strict YAML, no unfilled placeholders, name matches directory, both reference files linked so no orphans); whole-tree `--bundles-only` PASS (this skill clean; the single warning is a pre-existing `demo-capture` `.pyc` orphan, logged as a v3.15.3 Advisory); `run_trigger_evals.py --gate` PASS (0 un-allowlisted collisions, 0 routing failures across 7 skills with cases). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so the `make validate` steps were run individually. CI needs no edit: the new bundle flows through the existing `--bundles-only` + `--gate` + skill-security steps under the already-optimized `validate` job (path filter, concurrency cancel-in-progress, pip caching all present). Registration in the three `data/` files + the reverse-engineering-matrix row + the CHANGELOG entry are Phase 2. One minor deviation logged as NI-1: the 250-char cap fits 3 of the 5 plan-listed trigger phrases verbatim (the other two are in `overview_l1` + When-to-Use). Phases 2-3 pending.

## [2026-07-23] - v3.15.2 adoption-awesome-llm-apps Phase 4: behavioral-eval schema interop

Implemented Phase 4 of the awesome-llm-apps adoption plan on `feat/adoption-awesome-llm-apps` - interop between the `skill-eval-loop`'s behavioral evals and an external skill-eval schema. **4.1 (align-vs-adapter decision)**: compared the eval-loop's internal `evals.json` (a bare list of `{id, query, should_trigger, assertions:[{text}], tags?, turns?, trigger_turn?, model?}`) against the interoperable schema `{skill_name, evals:[{id, prompt, expected_output, expectations[]}]}`. Chose an ADAPTER over native re-alignment: the internal format is a strict SUPERSET (it carries `should_trigger` for the optimizer's trigger-rate metric, `turns`/`trigger_turn` for multi-turn testing, `model` for cheap-model fragility, and `tags`), so adopting the interoperable schema natively would drop those capabilities AND force a rewrite of the grader/aggregator/optimizer/viewer. A converter keeps every capability and changes nothing in the grading path. There is no committed sample `evals.json` (evals are authored per-workspace at runtime), so nothing to migrate. **4.2 (converter)**: added `scripts/skill_eval_convert.py`, stdlib-only (no third-party import, outbound call, or new dependency; cross-platform single .py, no .ps1 sibling, matching the sibling eval scripts). It maps `query`<->`prompt` and `assertions[].text`<->`expectations[]`, preserves a golden `expected_output` verbatim, and stashes every internal-only field (plus any assertion keys beyond `text`) under an `x_nexus` extension key so BOTH round-trips are lossless (`internal->interop->internal == internal`, `interop->internal->interop == interop`). CLI: `--to-interop` / `--to-internal`, `--skill-name`, `-o`, else stdout. Registered by explicit name in BOTH installers (sibling of aggregate_benchmark/skill_eval_viewer/optimize_skill_description); documented in `references/schemas.md` (a new interop section with the field mapping + the align-vs-adapter decision rationale, described generically with no external tool named) and referenced from the skill's SKILL.md via a new "Behavioral-eval schema interop" section. The grader/aggregator/optimizer/viewer and the internal format are UNTOUCHED, so grading is preserved by construction. **4.3 (tests + CI)**: `tests/validators/test_skill_eval_convert.py` (18 cases: query/assertions field mapping, extension-namespace behavior incl. assertion-extra-key preservation, both lossless round-trips, an already-`x_nexus`-carrying interop round-trip, expected_output-only-when-present, error handling for wrong-shape inputs, and CLI + in-process `main()` surfaces); converter line coverage 96%. Full `tests/validators` suite 302 passed; `--bundles-only` + trigger-evals `--gate` still PASS. No CI edit - the converter is a utility tested via the existing `pytest tests/validators` step, not a new gate. NO catalog-registry change (the SKILL.md edit is body-only; description/summary_l0 unchanged). No `base-*.md` or hook change. Phases 5-6 pending.

Added `--margin`; the JSON report gained a `routing` block; gate mode now exits non-zero on un-allowlisted collisions OR routing failures, while missing-cases never fails. **3.3 (first tranche)**: authored trigger-cases for 6 distinctive-noun skills - react-expert, vue-expert (the Phase 1 71% pair), gdpr-compliance, ccpa-compliance (56% pair), docx-generation (a `*-generation` sibling), and kubernetes-expert - each with 3 positives + 3 near-miss negatives drawn from sibling vocabulary. One iteration: the vue `neg-react` near-miss initially failed the margin because generic "component"/"state" words overlap both frameworks - retuned to "optimize react rendering with hooks" (react-distinctive), which is the eval correctly flagging a real lexical-overlap and the fix being a cleaner near-miss, not a description change. **3.4 (tests + CI)**: added routing tests to `tests/validators/test_run_trigger_evals.py` (rank-first pass, misroute, margin-fail, lexical-false skip, malformed-file discovery, no-cases WARN, JSON routing block, and a real-catalog tranche guard); runner line coverage 95%; two test-fixture corrections during authoring (a hand-written token set must use stemmer-stable words, since prompt tokens are stemmed). ## [2026-07-23] - v3.15.2 adoption-awesome-llm-apps Phase 2: unfilled-placeholder lint

Implemented Phase 2 of the awesome-llm-apps adoption plan on `feat/adoption-awesome-llm-apps` - a bounded regex fold-in to the existing skill validator so a scaffolded-but-unfinished skill cannot pass validation silently. **2.1 (detection)**: added `validate_placeholders` to `scripts/validate_skills.py` (plus the module regex `PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN` and two helpers `_strip_inline_code` / `_body_after_frontmatter`). A placeholder is a multi-word lowercase angle-bracket span - two or more single-space-separated lowercase words, hyphens allowed, e.g. `<what this skill does>` - matched by `<[a-z]+(?: [a-z-]+)+>`. It is a HARD ERROR in both the `description` frontmatter field and the SKILL.md body prose. The shape is deliberately tight so the real catalog stays at zero false positives: single-word CLI notation (`<path>`, `<name>`, `<category>`) has no interior space and is not matched; HTML tags (`<div>`, `<br/>`, `<a href="x">`) carry `=`/`"`/`/` and are excluded; uppercase template tokens (`<MAJOR>`, so `docs/v<MAJOR>/` is safe) are excluded; comparison operators (`x < y and y > z`) are excluded (a space follows `<`); and fenced code blocks + inline-code spans are skipped, with CommonMark-aware fence tracking mirrored from `scan_text_for_secrets` (a shorter inner fence cannot close a longer outer one, so a ` ```bash ` example inside a ` ````markdown ` block stays content). The description check strips inline code too, so a backticked example in a description is exempt. Wired into BOTH `validate_skill_dir` (full mode) and the `--bundles-only` branch that `make validate` and CI run, so the lint is enforced everywhere the strict-YAML gate is. **2.2 (triage)**: the first run over all 267 skills produced ZERO findings - no genuine unfilled scaffolds and no false positives - so no SKILL.md needed fixing (a positive/negative control confirmed the regex is not inert: it matches real placeholders and rejects every look-alike). **2.3 (tests + CI)**: added 14 cases to `tests/validators/test_validate_skills.py` (description hit, body hit, the CLI-notation / HTML / uppercase-token / comparison-operator negatives, the fenced / inline-code / backticked-description exemptions, a nested-fence guard using a 4-backtick outer fence, `_body_after_frontmatter` with and without frontmatter, and two end-to-end `--bundles-only` CLI tests - a scaffold skill that must exit 1 and a clean skill that must exit 0); new-code line coverage 100% in-process (the full-file 66% is the pre-existing subprocess-only `main()`, unchanged). Full `tests/validators` suite 272 passed; `--bundles-only` and `--quality` both PASS (0 errors) on the real catalog. NO CI edit needed - the check runs inside CI's existing `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` step and the tests run via the existing `pytest tests/validators` step; path filters and caching are unchanged (no redundant job). AGENTS.md documents the new lint alongside the orphan-bundle detection block. No installer, `base-*.md`, catalog-registry, or hook change. Phases 3-6 pending.

## [2026-07-23] - v3.15.2 adoption-awesome-llm-apps Phase 1: catalog-wide trigger-and-routing eval

Implemented Phase 1 of the awesome-llm-apps adoption plan on a fresh `feat/adoption-awesome-llm-apps` branch (cut off `develop`). The phase ships the catalog's first deterministic, model-free routing-safety gate: a skill-description near-collision detector. **1.1 (detector)**: new `scripts/run_trigger_evals.py` (Python stdlib only - `json`/`os`/`re`/`sys`/`argparse` - no third-party imports, no outbound call, no new dependency; the frontmatter parser is mirrored from `validate_skills.py` so the script is self-contained at its installed location). It tokenizes every skill's `description` (lowercase, split on non-alphanumerics, drop a stopword set that includes the "pushy-description" scaffolding vocabulary plus tokens under 3 chars, light suffix-stem ing/es/ed/s with a floor guard), then scores every pair with a containment metric `|A n B| / min(|A|, |B|)` - deliberately not Jaccard, so a smaller skill's vocabulary being subsumed by a larger one's still fires - and flags any pair at or above a configurable threshold (default 0.5). It supports `--threshold`, `--json`, `--allowlist`, and a `--gate`/`--strict` mode; default is WARNING-ONLY (always exit 0) so first-run findings are triaged before it becomes a merge gate. Generic descriptive names throughout per the reverse-engineering attribution rule (no external repo/product/author named). **1.2 (triage)**: the first run over all 267 skills surfaced 39 near-collisions. 38 are by-design category siblings (parallel `<lang>-cleanup` / `<lang>-expert` / `init-<lang>-project` / framework-expert / `*-generation` / mobile-platform / compliance-regulation pairs, and two matched pairs that already carry mutual SKIP clauses), routed apart by a domain noun that is the user's actual trigger. The one genuine collision was `technical-documentation` (a broad doc skill that advertised "ADRs" and had NO SKIP clause) colliding with the single-artifact `architecture-decision-record` and `project-constitution` skills; it was FIXED by sharpening `technical-documentation`'s description to defer to both via an explicit SKIP clause (kept under the 250-char ceiling), with the `data/skills.json` `description` mirror updated to match (`summary_l0` and `SKILL_INDEX.md` untouched - the detector reads only `description`). **1.3 (allowlist)**: `scripts/run_trigger_evals.allowlist.json` (modeled on `validate_skills.allowlist.json`) records the 39 intentional near-neighbor pairs, each with a one-line justification; the runner downgrades them to informational lines, and `--gate` now reports zero un-allowlisted collisions. **1.4 (registration)**: registered warning-first in BOTH installers (`installer.sh` + `installer.ps1`, next to the eval-loop dispatcher scripts, copying the script and its allowlist to `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/`), the `Makefile` (a `trigger-evals` target plus a warning-only step inside `validate`), and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (a warning-only step in the `validate` job). **1.5 (tests + CI)**: `tests/validators/test_run_trigger_evals.py` (25 tests: tokenizer/stemmer, containment metric, threshold floor, allowlist downgrade, warning-only vs `--gate` exit codes, a colliding fixture pair the detector must catch and a distinct pair it must not, plus in-process `main()` coverage and a real-catalog zero-un-allowlisted guard) - 96% line coverage on the new script; CI auto-runs them via the existing `pytest tests/validators` step. Full `tests/validators` suite 258 passed; shellcheck on `installer.sh` clean; `skills.json` valid (267 skills). CI/CD is already optimized (concurrency cancel-in-progress, pip caching, cost-gated matrix legs), so the eval rides the existing `validate` job as a sub-second step rather than a separately-path-filtered job (DF-1). Promotion from warning-only to a hard `--gate` is deferred to Phase 6. No `base-*.md`, catalog-command, or hook change. Phases 2-6 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 6: knowledge-map extractor

Implemented Phase 6 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - a deterministic knowledge-map extractor over a folder of Markdown notes, emitting a committed `.nexus/KNOWLEDGE.md`. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. **Re-confirmed decision (the plan asked to re-decide at implementation)**: ship as extension code, NOT a new catalog skill - consistent with the Phase 5.2 lint decision, the mechanical value is real (a committed cold-start knowledge primer), and the narrative synthesis stays with the LLM-native `solution-knowledge-base` skill. This keeps Phases 1-6 entirely extension-only (no `data/` change, no `make validate`). **6.1 extractor** (`contextmap/knowledge.py`): scans `.md` notes (graph-independent - it reads Markdown, not `codegraph.db`), classifies each by a weighted filename (3) / heading (2) / body (1) signal score into decision / meeting / retro / spec / research (else a plain note), and extracts key decisions (the paragraph under a `## Decision` heading or a decision-verb line), open questions (items under an Open Questions heading + standalone `TODO`/`TBD`/`FIXME` lines), and a categorized note index -> `.nexus/KNOWLEDGE.md`. ## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 5: token-savings benchmark + map-health lint

Implemented Phase 5 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - the measurement + health phase that validates the measured half of the definition of done. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. **5.1 token-savings benchmark** (`contextmap/benchmark.py` + committed `benchmark_baseline.json`, patterned on `nexus-context-compressor/evals`): measures the compiled map's token count against a SIMULATED manual-exploration cost - the sum of per-file tokens times a documented revisit multiplier (an AI re-reads files while exploring) plus a per-entity discovery overhead for each route / model / component / env var. The reduction ratio is `1 - map_cost / manual_cost`; the estimation constants are the tool's own heuristic. The map cost is computed WITHOUT writing `.nexus/` (a new `estimate_map_tokens` in the generator renders in memory) and each repo indexes into a throwaway directory, so benchmarking never mutates the repo it measures. A key honest finding: the tiny per-framework `contextmap` fixtures show NEGATIVE savings (a map is not worth its fixed overhead on a 2-file repo), so the benchmark corpus is three realistic committed sample repos (`shop_api`, `blog_ts`, `tasks_py`) that show 44-55% reduction, plus a run on Nexus-Hub itself: a ~22k-token map replaces ~1.9M tokens of manual exploration (~99% reduction across 443 files). `benchmark_baseline.json` records a per-repo floor (a margin below the measured ratio) so a regression - the map silently losing its savings - fails `--check`; `--update-baseline` re-baselines intentionally. **5.2 map-health lint** (`contextmap/maphealth.py`): deterministic checks for orphan articles (not linked from the index), missing backlinks (article not linking `../CONTEXT-MAP.md`), and staleness (the map's embedded source fingerprint vs a freshly-recomputed one - I extracted the fingerprint into a shared `current_source_hash` so the lint and the generator agree exactly). Exposed as the `map_health` MCP tool and `nexus-hub map --lint` (exit 1 when unhealthy). **Decision**: the lint ships as extension code, NOT a new catalog skill - the richer semantic checks stay in the LLM-native `documentation-consistency` skill - so no `data/` registry files were touched (Phases 1-5 remain entirely extension-only). **5.3 tests**: `test_context_map_measurement.py` (19) covers the benchmark (positive reduction, corpus-meets-baseline, seeded-regression gate, side-effect-free, CLI `--json`/`--check`/`--repo`/missing-corpus, `measured_baseline` floors) and the lint (healthy, seeded orphan/backlink/stale, no-map, CLI exit codes, the MCP handler). **Gates**: full extension suite 285 passed / 1 skipped (+19 Phase 5 tests), new-code coverage 94% (contextmap; benchmark.py lifted to 90% after CLI tests), all new/modified code ruff-clean. The benchmark + lint run in CI via the existing pytest job (no CI edit needed). Known-gaps: both DoD axes now hold; MT-2 added (`--update-baseline` write path untested by design). Phases 6-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 4: hot files + git-scoped change map

Implemented Phase 4 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - graph enrichment: file-level hot-file ranking and a git-scoped `--since` change map. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. Both sub-tasks reuse the existing reverse-import machinery in `graph/affected.py`. **4.1 hot files**: added `most_imported_files(conn, limit)` to `graph/affected.py` - it inverts the same import-resolution rules `affected_tests` uses (loading import nodes once, matching in Python) to rank files by inbound import count. The generator loads the top 25 into the model and fills the map's "Most-Imported Files" section (previously a Phase 1 placeholder), rendered as a `File | Imported by` table with a note that it is a FILE-level view distinct from the symbol-level `code_impact` blast radius (so the two never read as competing "impact" numbers). `GENERATOR_VERSION` bumped 3 -> 4; this resolves the outstanding half of DF-1 (the frameworks half shipped in Phase 2). **4.2 `--since <ref>`**: a new `contextmap/changemap.py` runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` and produces a `ChangeMap` - the changed files plus the affected routes (whose source/handler file changed), affected models (source changed), affected symbols (significant nodes declared in changed files), and the transitively affected test files (the existing `affected_tests` reverse-import BFS). ## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 3: ORM schema + components + events

Implemented Phase 3 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - the framework-extraction II pass (schema + components + events), the plan's hardest phase (ORM relation resolution). Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. Consistent with Phase 2, everything is post-graph source parsing inside `contextmap/` (no new extraction-time resolvers). **3.1 schema** (`schema.py`): ORM models with fields, PK/FK/unique flags, and relations across SQLAlchemy (`Column`/`mapped_column` + `relationship()`), Django ORM (`models.XField` + ForeignKey/OneToOne/ManyToMany), and Prisma (`.prisma` DSL `model` blocks). Class-based ORMs are located from the `class` nodes already in the graph and parsed from their source span (a helper joins multi-line field defs until parens balance); Prisma is parsed from the `.prisma` files. Detection keys on ORM-specific tokens (`models.Model`/`models.X(`, `Column(`/`relationship(`), so a plain class (or a Django `Meta`) is never mistaken for a model - the fixtures include a decoy class to lock that. Relations carry name + target + best-effort kind (Django FK->many-to-one, M2M->many-to-many; Prisma `[]`->one-to-many else many-to-one; SQLAlchemy relationship()->relation). **3.2 components + events** (`components.py`, `events.py`): React components are detected in `.tsx`/`.jsx` as exported PascalCase function/const declarations (JSX-file scoping makes that a reliable signal, so a plain helper or a hook is not misreported), with props unioned from the destructured parameter AND the resolved prop type (a `}: Props` annotation or a `React.FC<Props>` generic resolved to its `interface`/`type` in the same file). Events detect declaration-strong background-work surfaces only (Celery task decorators, BullMQ `new Queue/Worker`, Kafka, `new EventEmitter`), deferring FP-prone invocation-only patterns (`.delay(`/`.emit(`/`.publish(`). **Map**: Data Models / Components / Events sections + a `database` article with per-model field/relation detail; `GENERATOR_VERSION` 2 -> 3; the source fingerprint now also covers `.prisma` files (a schema change invalidates the no-op). **3.3 accuracy** (`accuracy.py` extended + `schema_app`/`frontend_app` fixtures): `evaluate()` now scores only the sections a fixture declares (so the Phase 2 route fixtures are untouched) and adds models / relations / components / events; a dedicated `test_relation_resolution` asserts 100% relation recall with zero FP across Django, SQLAlchemy, and Prisma. Two component-props bugs were found and fixed via the fixtures: a single-line `type X = {...}` only yielded its first member (fixed by splitting on member separators), and a `React.FC<CardProps>` component whose arrow only destructures a subset now unions in the full declared prop type. **Gates**: full extension suite 257 passed / 1 skipped (+12 Phase 3 tests), new-code coverage 95% (contextmap), all new/modified code ruff-clean. CI needs no edit (path-filtered `code-search.yml` + always-on `tests` job auto-discover the new tests/fixtures). Known-gaps: DF-3 expanded to record the deferred ORMs (TypeORM/Drizzle/ActiveRecord/GORM), component libs (Vue/Svelte), and event patterns as explicit coverage. Phases 4-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 2: framework routes + env audit + middleware

Implemented Phase 2 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - framework-aware route extraction, an env-var audit, and middleware detection, all feeding the compiled context map and gated by an extraction-accuracy harness. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. **Architecture (reuse-first)**: rather than adding new extraction-time resolvers, Phase 2 reads the `route` nodes the EXISTING FastAPI / Flask / Django / Express resolvers already emit (built in v2.2.0-v2.3.0) and enriches them in a read-only post-graph layer. **2.1 routes** (`contextmap/routes.py` + `behavior.py`): parses each route node into framework / method / path / URL params (unioning `{x}`, `<conv:x>`, `:x`, and `(?P<x>)` syntaxes), resolves the handler via the `decorates` / `references` edge, and infers coarse behavior tags (auth / db / cache / payment / ai / queue / email) from the handler's source. A key refinement: when no handler edge resolves (an Express inline arrow handler has no separate node), tags are inferred from the route node's OWN source span, so inline handlers are still tagged - the FastAPI decorator span (body lives elsewhere) uses the edge-based handler slice instead, and unioning both covers both styles without adding false positives. Behavior tokens are deliberately distinctive (library/API surface names, word-boundary-anchored) so a generic verb does not trigger a tag. **2.2 env + middleware** (`env.py`, `middleware.py`): the env audit scans indexed source for real env-access forms (`os.environ[...]`, `os.getenv(...)`, `process.env.X`, `import.meta.env`) and classifies each required vs has-default (a default at the call site, or an `.env.example` declaration, means not-required), and merges NAMES from `.env.example`-style files (never the real `.env`, never a value); middleware detection finds `app.use(...)` / `add_middleware(...)` / Django `MIDDLEWARE=[...]` registrations and categorizes each (auth / rate-limit / cors / validation / logging / error-handling / other) by a conservative name match. Both reject look-alikes (a plain `dict["X"]` is not an env var). **Map**: the generator gained Routes / Environment / Middleware sections + a `context/routes.md` article + an Overview `Frameworks:` line (resolving the frameworks half of Phase 1's DF-1); `GENERATOR_VERSION` bumped 1 -> 2 (format change invalidates old maps) and the source fingerprint now covers `.env.example` files so a change to one invalidates the no-op. **2.3 accuracy harness** (`accuracy.py` + `tests/fixtures/contextmap/{fastapi,express,django}_app` with hand-counted `truth.json`): per-section recall + a HARD zero-false-positive gate; `test_context_map_accuracy.py` enforces both. The harness immediately earned its keep - it flagged a "false positive" on the Django fixture (`ANY admin/`) that was actually a ground-truth omission on my part (`path("admin/", include(...))` binds both `admin/` and the include), which I corrected. **Gates**: full extension suite 245 passed / 1 skipped (+23 Phase 2 tests), new-code coverage 95% (contextmap package), all new/modified code ruff-clean. CI needs no edit - the path-filtered `code-search.yml` and the always-on `tests` job both auto-discover the new tests and fixtures. Known-gaps ([docs/v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md](v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md)): DF-1 frameworks half resolved (most-imported still Phase 4), DF-3 added (additional route frameworks Hono/Fastify/Next/NestJS/Gin/Rails/Spring/Laravel + ORMs deferred as explicit coverage, per the plan's incremental posture). Phases 3-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 1: compiled context-map generator + `nexus-hub map`

Implemented Phase 1 of the v3.15.1 CodeSight-adoption plan on a fresh `feat/adoption-codesight` branch (cut off `develop`, chosen over the current `feat/platform-parity-all-gaps` branch which holds a different, complete v3.15.0 feature set). The whole phase is extension-only, inside `extensions/nexus-code-search/`: it compiles the tree-sitter AST graph the extension already builds (`codegraph.db`: files / nodes / edges) into a deterministic, committed `.nexus/CONTEXT-MAP.md` plus a `.nexus/context/` article set, so an AI reads a cheap cold-start map once instead of re-exploring files every session. **1.1 (generator)**: new `contextmap/` package - `model.py` (rendering-free content model + a SHA-256 source fingerprint over the sorted `(path, content_hash)` rows), `tokens.py` (a `count_tokens` that prefers tiktoken/cl100k_base but falls back to a stdlib heuristic, so no new dependency and the zero-outbound posture holds), and `generator.py` (reads the graph, groups files by top-level module, counts significant symbols, and renders the map + an `index.md` + one article per module). Three load-bearing guarantees, each test-locked: **neutral path** (every write is confined to `<root>/.nexus/` via an `is_relative_to` guard; AI-config files are never touched), **deterministic** (no wall-clock timestamp in the output, so the MCP tool and the CLI are byte-identical for the same graph), and **content-hash incremental** (the source fingerprint is embedded in the map; an unchanged graph is a no-op unless `force`). The token-count header every output file carries is measured over the document EXCLUDING its own metadata line, dodging the circular-count problem. The "Most-Imported Files" section and an Overview frameworks line are explicit Phase-1 placeholders (Phase 4 / Phase 2 respectively; DF-1). **1.2 (surfaces)**: added the `generate_context_map` MCP tool to `server.py` (tool def + dispatch + handler + instructions) and wired a `nexus-hub map [root] [--force] [--json]` verb into `scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py` - verified the dispatcher wiring first, and because the map logic lives entirely in the extension and `nexus_hub_cli.py` is already installer-copied, NO installer edit was needed (the ask-first gate was not tripped); the verb forwards verbatim to `nexus_code_search.contextmap.cli`, mirroring the `nexus_hub_affected.py` late-import + pip-hint precedent. **1.3 (tests + CI)**: `tests/test_context_map.py` (22 tests: sections, per-file token-header accuracy, neutral-path, no-op vs force vs graph-change, tool-vs-CLI byte-identity, empty-graph, missing-graph exit codes, and the tiktoken-preference + fallback paths) and a new path-filtered `.github/workflows/code-search.yml` (scoped to `extensions/nexus-code-search/**`, pip-cached, concurrency cancel-in-progress). **Gates**: full extension suite green (222 passed, 1 pre-existing skip), new-code coverage 97%, all new/modified code ruff-clean (the one ruff finding is a PRE-EXISTING unused `json` import in `nexus_hub_cli.py`, left out of scope and logged as WN-1), workflow-security + IOC validators exit 0. Known-gaps recorded in [docs/v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md](v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md): DF-1 (placeholders), DF-2 (extension version not bumped), WN-1, MT-1 (repo-level dispatch not auto-tested), QG-1 (extension tests run in both ci.yml and code-search.yml - Phase 7 CI-optimization to de-dupe), QG-2 (three plans share v3.15.0 - reconcile before release). No catalog registry files, installers, or `base-*.md` templates touched. Phases 2-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.0 Phase 3: OpenCode parity (agents surface; plugins/hooks out of scope)

Implemented Phase 3 (OpenCode parity) of the v3.15.0 platform-parity plan on `feat/platform-parity-all-gaps`. Contract updated: `parity_verification_v3_15_0.opencode` (agents `phase3_delivered` + plugins `phase3_decision`), `contract_checks.opencode.doc_mentions` + `install_verify` gained the agents path, and the `.md` Re-verification log carries the 2026-07-21 Phase 3 entry. **Validation**: `test_opencode.py` 6/6; ruff clean; full `tests/integrations` green; `verify_platform_contracts.py` OK (8 platforms - adding agents to `doc_mentions` is consistent with the new config); workspace + global dry-runs land agents at the verified paths and write no hooks. ## [2026-07-20] - v3.14.7: usage-monitor status-bar icon spacing

Small cosmetic follow-up to v3.14.6, driven by the user noticing (in the shipped v3.14.6 extensions) that the status-bar icon sat glued to the usage text - `icon47% (current)...` with no gap. Root cause: VS Code collapses consecutive plain spaces in a status-bar label, so the single separating space in `${ICON} ${label}...` did not survive rendering. Fix (both extensions, lockstep): each `statusBarManager.ts` now defines a module-level `const ICON_GAP = "\u2002"` (an en-space, U+2002, which does NOT collapse) and places it between the icon and the label in every `statusText` branch - Codex's no-data path (`${CODEX_ICON}${ICON_GAP}${label}--${staleLabel}`) and data path, and Claude's compact and full paths. Written as the ASCII `\u2002` escape (not a literal en-space char) to keep the source ASCII-clean and avoid the invisible-character fragility that `validate_unicode_safety` guards against. The test friction was purely tooling: the Edit tool and bash heredocs kept rendering my `\u2002` intent as either a literal en-space or a normal space, so I used Python (`chr(0x2002)` to search, `chr(92)+"u2002"` for the replacement text) to write the exact escape deterministically, verified via `repr()` and `line.isascii()`. Both extensions' `statusBarManager.test.ts` expected strings updated from `"$(icon) ..."` to `"$(icon)\u2002..."` (4 occurrences Codex, 2 Claude). Extension versions bumped Claude 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3, Codex 0.2.3 -> 0.2.4; user verified the gap renders correctly in the live host before release. Verification: both type-clean (`tsc` exit 0), Vitest green (Codex 43, Claude 5), both VSIXes packaged. Platform read-contract reaffirmed (not re-verified) - v3.14.7 touched no platform read-paths, so the 2026-07-19 full re-verification holds; freshness marker re-stamped to 3.14.7. Catalog counts unchanged (267 skills, 16 commands, 28 hooks).

## [2026-07-20] - v3.14.6: Codex auto-fetch fix, inline settings, installer-log overhaul

Post-v3.14.5 fix release driven by user testing of the shipped v3.14.5 extensions. **Codex auto-fetch root-caused and fixed**: the monitor showed "No Usage Data" even though the token + endpoint were fine. Probing `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` live (with the user's `~/.codex/auth.json` token, on their machine) returned HTTP 200 - the failure was a mapper schema mismatch. Our `locateWindows` looked for `rate_limits` (plural) with `primary`/`secondary`; the real response nests the windows under `rate_limit` (singular) as `primary_window`/`secondary_window`, and the user's Team plan exposes a single 7-day (weekly) window (`limit_window_seconds: 604800`, `secondary_window: null`). Rewrote the mapper to the verified schema and made it classify each window by its own duration (so a weekly-only window maps to weekly, not mislabeled "current session"); retired the "undocumented endpoint" caveat (DF-2). **Manual entry removed** (per user): the command, dashboard button, and prompts are gone now that auto-fetch works; the empty state is an honest fetch-failure diagnostic. **Both extensions: settings moved inline** - the status-bar gear item is removed and the dashboard's gear now toggles a Settings section rendered under the dashboard (state-persisted across re-renders via `vscode.getState`, unified fonts/headings), replacing the standalone settings webview; the shared settings form was extracted into an embeddable module (`settingsPanel.ts` exports CSS/HTML/JS builders + save/reset) that the dashboard stitches into its single webview. **Status-bar order fixed**: with the gear gone, the two usage items sit in a band above GitHub Copilot's ~100.5 slot so Copilot no longer wedges between them. **Installer log overhaul** (`installer.ps1` + `installer.sh`, lockstep): flat `> UPPERCASE` main sections (dropped the "Global Installation" super-header + the double blank after the welcome), "Usage Monitors" renamed "VS CODE EXTENSIONS", skill discovery + git hook + report templates grouped under a new "CROSS-PLATFORM TOOLS" section, project seeding folded under "INSTALL VERIFICATION", stray double-blank spacing removed, and the workspace path made consistent (its "Workspace install" super-header became a "SKILLS & COMMANDS" main section, with the CROSS-PLATFORM TOOLS header emitted before templates so the workspace path is not orphaned). **Branch hygiene**: the v3.14.6 work had been layered on `feat/platform-parity-all-gaps` (the in-progress v3.15.0 branch) atop uncommitted v3.15.0 Phase 1.2 work; separated cleanly - the v3.15.0 WIP (cursor parity + contract records) was committed on its own branch (a56cdffa), and only the v3.14.6 extension + installer changes were moved to `fix/usage-monitor-and-installer-ux` off develop. Verification: both extensions type-clean (Codex 43 Vitest, Claude 5), installer.ps1 parses clean, `bash -n` + ShellCheck clean, installer smoke 29/29. Platform read-contract reaffirmed (not re-verified) - v3.14.6 changed no platform read-paths, so the 2026-07-19 full re-verification holds; freshness marker re-stamped to 3.14.6. Catalog counts unchanged (267 skills, 16 commands, 28 hooks).

## [2026-07-19] - v3.14.5 Phase 1: runner structured per-surface results

Implemented Phase 1 of the v3.14.5 installer-ux-and-monitor-fixes plan on `feat/installer-ux-monitor-fixes` (cut off `develop`). This is the foundation the rest of the installer-UX work stands on: it teaches `scripts/lib/integrations/runner.py` to emit a structured, per-platform, per-surface install summary even under `--quiet`, so the Phase 2 checklist can render real checkmarks and paths instead of the current unconditional "Installed (global scope)" line - which is also why undetected Kimi/Qwen/OpenClaw currently look installed. **1.1/1.2 (summary channel)**: added an opt-in `--summary-json PATH` to the `install` subcommand plus `_classify_surface` (maps a `FileAction` path to a canonical surface - instruction/skills/commands/agents/rules/hooks/settings - by path shape, so it captures a surface regardless of how each integration computed the path, e.g. Codex delivering commands via `prompts/`), `_common_path` (representative path per surface), and `_build_platform_summary`. `cmd_install` builds the summary directly from each integration's `WriteResult`, so it is populated regardless of `--quiet`; existing stdout is byte-identical when `--summary-json` is not passed (a deliberate DEVIATION from the plan's "modify `_render_write_result` wording - that early-return only suppresses PRINTING, not the data, so reading the `WriteResult` in hand is lower-risk). **1.3 (detection state)**: added `WriteResult.detected: Optional[bool]` + a `mark_not_detected()` helper (sets the flag AND appends the existing note) + detection propagation through `extend()`, and flipped the five detection-gated subclasses (kimi/qwen/openclaw/windsurf/copilot) to call it on their skip branch and set `detected = True` on the positive path. **Testing / troubleshooting (1 iteration)**: new `tests/integrations/test_install_summary.py` (25 tests: classifier, common-path, `mark_not_detected`/`extend`, summary builder, and `cmd_install --summary-json` detected/undetected/quiet) is green. The first full `tests/integrations` run was 326 passed / 2 failed - both `'_StubIntegration' object has no attribute 'key'` in `test_runner_target_root.py`, from `_build_platform_summary` reading `integ.key`; root-caused as needless coupling (the runner already holds the authoritative key) and fixed by `_build_platform_summary(key, integ, result)` with `getattr(integ, "display_name", key)`, fixing both without editing that test; the two affected files then pass 32/32 and the full suite is green. An end-to-end dry-run confirms kimi/qwen report `detected: false` with no surfaces while codex/cursor/opencode report their real classified surfaces. **Lint**: ruff is not a project gate (no config; not in the Makefile or CI); the one ruff finding is a pre-existing unused `FileAction` import in `qwen.py` (confirmed via `git show HEAD`), left untouched per the no-out-of-scope-cleanup rule and logged as WN-1. Per the runbook, the version bump / changelog / merge / tag are deferred to `/update release`; no CHANGELOG version finalize here. Phases 2-7 (installer checklist + undetected grouping + colors; end-of-run spacing + vendor-split utilities; Codex monitor data + icon; cross-extension status bar + compact mode; contract-freshness gate; terminal refactor) pending.

## [2026-07-16] - v3.14.1 Phase 2: orphaned auth-monitor scheduled-task cleanup

Implemented Phase 2 of the v3.14.1 installer-hotfix plan on `fix/installer-hotfix`. Fixes the second half of the user report: DevAI-Hub v0.9.x registered a user-level Windows scheduled task named exactly "Claude Code Auth Monitor" that ran `wscript.exe "...\.devai-hub\scripts\run-auth-monitor.vbs"` every two minutes; the auth monitor and the `~/.devai-hub/` tree were later removed but nothing unregistered the task, so it still fires against a missing `.vbs` and pops a recurring "Can not find script file" Windows Script Host dialog. **2.1 (task cleanup)**: added `_cleanup_windows_auth_monitor_task(ctx)` to `scripts/lib/integrations/legacy.py`, modeled on the existing `_cleanup_claude_legacy_vscode_extension` subprocess pattern. It returns `None` (no-op) when not on Windows (`os.name != "nt"`), when `schtasks` is not on PATH, when `schtasks /Query /TN "Claude Code Auth Monitor"` exits non-zero (task absent, the normal case), or when the query/delete subprocess raises; otherwise it deletes the task with `schtasks /Delete /TN ... /F` (dry-run returns the `FileAction` without mutating). The task is user-level, so no elevation is needed. Added `import os`. **2.2 (leftover launcher sweep)**: added two sibling cleanups `_cleanup_devai_hub_auth_monitor_vbs` and `_cleanup_devai_hub_auth_monitor_ps1` that `_remove_path_if_exists` on `~/.devai-hub/scripts/run-auth-monitor.vbs` and `claude-auth-monitor.ps1` (belt-and-suspenders; the tree is usually already gone). They never remove the whole `~/.devai-hub/` - that stays gated on `~/.nexus-hub/` existing in `_cleanup_devai_hub_legacy_global_dir`. Registered all three under `LEGACY_CLEANUPS["claude"]` after the existing three, so `run_cleanups` reports one `FileAction` per artifact actually removed. Chose three sibling single-artifact functions over one combined function because `CleanupFn` returns a single `Optional[FileAction]` and per-artifact reporting is the run_cleanups contract. **2.3 (tests)**: extended `tests/integrations/test_legacy_cleanups.py` with nine cases - task present -> removed + `/Delete` invoked; task absent -> None, no delete; off-Windows -> None, no subprocess; no `schtasks` -> None; dry-run -> `FileAction` without delete; idempotency (second pass returns None); and vbs / ps1 leftover removal (asserting the `~/.devai-hub/` tree survives the sweep) plus an absent-leftover no-op. The schtasks cases monkeypatch `legacy.os.name`, `legacy.shutil.which`, and `legacy.subprocess.run`, so they exercise the Windows branch deterministically on the Linux CI runner (the function constructs no `Path`, so patching `os.name = "nt"` is safe). Module suite 20 passed; full `tests/integrations/` suite green (the three new cleanups no-op on a clean CI system, so existing tests are unaffected). ruff clean. No CI change (same rationale as Phase 1: the existing `tests` job already runs `pytest tests/integrations`). Installer-side only in `scripts/lib/integrations/`; auto-distributes via the integration-registry folder copy, no installer copy-step edit, no `base-*.md` change. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` gained the Issue 2 Fixed entry with the manual `Unregister-ScheduledTask` one-liner. Phase 3 (refactor + known-gaps + CI/CD, then `/update release`) pending.

## [2026-07-16] - v3.14.1 Phase 1: global-install manifest path + graceful degradation

Implemented Phase 1 of the v3.14.1 installer-hotfix plan on `fix/installer-hotfix` (cut off the freshly-released v3.14.0 on `develop`). Fixes a real user report: a global install run from an elevated `C:\Windows\System32` prompt emitted a `PermissionError [WinError 5]` traceback for every integration because the runner's target-root fallback resolved the manifest under the CWD (`C:\Windows\System32\.nexus-hub\`) instead of the user home. **1.1 (scope-aware fallback)**: added a single `_resolve_target_root(args) -> Path` helper to `scripts/lib/integrations/runner.py` with precedence explicit-`--target` > `--scope global` -> `Path.home()` > `Path.cwd()`, and replaced all nine inline `Path(args.target)... else Path.cwd()` occurrences (`_template_vars_from_args`, `cmd_install`, `cmd_print_config`, `cmd_check`, `cmd_init`, `cmd_doctor`, `cmd_repair`, `cmd_list_installed`, `cmd_verify`) with it; `cmd_teardown`'s required-`--target` line is untouched, and subcommands with no `--scope` flag keep their CWD default (`getattr(args,"scope",None)` is `None`). Corrected the `install --target` help text (it wrongly said global was "ignored"). **1.2 (graceful degradation)**: wrapped `manifest.save(...)` in `cmd_install` and `cmd_teardown` in `try/except OSError`, emitting one stderr warning and continuing rather than aborting the runner with a traceback and non-zero exit; the manifest is bookkeeping for upgrade / doctor / repair, so its failure must not mask an otherwise-successful install. **1.3 (tests + CI + changelog)**: new `tests/integrations/test_runner_target_root.py` (7 tests: global -> home with the manifest under home not CWD, workspace -> CWD, explicit target wins for both scopes, missing-scope-attr -> CWD, `cmd_install` global + foreign CWD writes under home and exits 0, and a `PermissionError`-on-save -> return 0 + warning). ruff clean; new module 7/7 pass; full `tests/integrations/` suite green (no regressions - workspace/existing behavior preserved). No CI change: the existing `tests` job already runs `pytest tests/integrations` on non-docs changes with `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` set, so a dedicated path-filtered job would only duplicate work and raise action minutes (Phase 3.3 revisits CI). Installer-side only, in `scripts/lib/integrations/`, so the fix auto-distributes via the integration-registry folder copy with no installer copy-step edit and no `base-*.md` change. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` gained the Fixed entries. Phase 2 (orphaned auth-monitor scheduled-task cleanup) and Phase 3 (refactor + known-gaps + CI/CD + `/update release`) pending.

## [2026-07-16] - v3.14.0 Phase 5: cross-model review recipe concretization (C2)

Implemented Phase 5 of the v3.14.0 codex-lb-adoption plan on `feat/codex-lb-adoption`: a single body-only extension to `catalog/skills/orchestration/cross-model-orchestrator/SKILL.md`, concretizing Nexus-Hub's already-strong cross-model story into a runnable, model-agnostic loop-until-clean review recipe adapted from codex-lb's `codex-review-loop` but generalized off any single vendor. New "Cross-Model Review Loop" section: (1) resolve scope (PR / base branch / uncommitted diff, captured once); (2) launch the review on a DIFFERENT operator-configured model as a background subagent in a fresh session, never a hardcoded vendor, with the existing Handoff Egress Hygiene gate applied when it reaches an external service; (3) parse the raw review into a documented findings schema (id / severity / category / location / effort / status); (4) a HITL disposition gate (fix all / criticals-only / report-only) before any code change; (5) an atomic per-finding fix-verify-commit cycle (apply, run lint/type/tests, commit only on pass, roll back on failure, one finding per commit) framed as the `verification-before-completion` gate applied per finding; (6) re-review with explicit SAFETY LIMITS (max 3 iterations; a finding whose id recurs across two iterations is marked do-not-refix and surfaced, so the loop always terminates); (7) a final report that states plainly when the iteration cap was hit. Vendor-neutrality is stated explicitly and cited to the MCP Registry Policy generation-as-service hard-no: the recipe adopts the loop's SHAPE, not a Codex-CLI lock-in, driving whatever review CLI the operator configures via an env var (documented inline, arg-array invocation per the Bash security rules). Decided NOT to bundle a wrapper script - the fix-verify-commit loop is inherently agent-driven, so a wrapper would only thinly wrap `git diff | $configured_CLI` while forcing a cross-platform `.sh`/`.ps1` pair; the invocation is documented inline instead, and the skill notes that a shipped wrapper would live under `scripts/` calling the operator's configured CLI. Added a vendor-neutrality Common Rationalizations row and cross-links to `multi-agent-code-review`, `adversarial-verifier`, `receiving-code-review`, and `verification-before-completion`. ## [2026-07-11] - v3.12.0 Phase 4: presentify design-entropy engine (seeded rolls + run history)

Implemented Phase 4 of the presentify-fidelity-and-variety plan: the fix for "running presentify twice with the same preset converges to the same look". The insight the phase encodes: unseeded taste converges - an LLM sampling its own prior lands on the same palette and layout run after run - so variety has to be MECHANICAL first and judgment second. New stdlib-only `scripts/design_seed.py` (~470 lines, no dependencies, no network): curated axis pools - 12 hue families spanning the wheel, each with a LIGHT and a DARK base variant plus two curated accents (so preset constraints never collapse the light/dark axis), 8 palette moods, 8 system-stack type voices, 10 layout signatures with one-line descriptions the agent adapts from (bento-mosaic, spine-timeline, offset-column-rhythm, diagonal-stagger...), 4 motion personalities, 8 signature interactive moves, 3 spacing rhythms. Preset subsets keep intent (technical excludes saturated-playful/soft-pastel moods and serif-display voices; corporate constrains mood, not hue; surprise gets everything). Entropy: `os.urandom` seed by default, `--seed N` for exact reproduction. History: rolled briefs are appended (after actual use) via `--commit` to `~/.nexus-hub/state/presentify-design-history.json` (capped at 40; corrupt file degrades to a fresh start with a warning), and each roll generates `--candidates` (default 3), REJECTS any candidate sharing 2+ of {hue family, layout signature, type voice} with any of the last 3 committed runs, widens to the full pools once if everything is rejected, and picks the accepted candidate maximizing axis distance from recent history. The dark+amber+mono attractor combination is guard-rejected under every named preset (reachable only under surprise at 5% odds, as a deliberate rare pick).

Wiring: `references/interactive-features.md`'s design-direction flow gained step 3 "Roll the design brief - mechanical entropy FIRST, judgment second" (usage, the no-silent-re-roll rule, `--commit`, the no-Python manual-variation fallback), the brainstorm section was reframed from generate-candidates to adapt-the-brief, and the token-commitment record now includes the roll's seed + one-line summary. SKILL.md's design step gained the roll bullet, a new rationalization row ("I have good taste, I don't need the roll"), and two verification items (seed + summary in the design record with tokens matching the brief's axes; history advanced via --commit or the fallback stated). The `/presentify` command's design-menu section explains that choosing the same preset twice still yields a different palette, type voice, and layout.

Validation (`docs/v3/v3.12/development/fixtures/verify_design_seed.py`, committed; temp-dir history, never the user's): 10/10 checks PASS - five sequential committed technical-preset runs never share 2+ of the triple axes and span 4+ hue families; `--seed 42` reproduces byte-identical briefs and a different seed differs; the history caps at 40 entries and a corrupt file recovers with a warning (exit 0); 60 seeded technical rolls stay inside the preset's mood/voice subsets while covering both light and dark bases; 240 seeded rolls across the three named presets never produce the attractor combo; every brief carries concrete hexes, CSS stacks, and a summary. Bundle audit 0 errors (design_seed.py referenced from SKILL.md), unicode 0 errors, ruff clean. Installer-neutral (bundle `scripts/` auto-copied); no registry change; no new outbound call, dependency, or credential.
