## [2026-07-11] - v3.12.0 Phase 2: presentify figure-reconstruction protocol (worksheets, confidence gate, OCR verification)

Implemented Phase 2 of the presentify-fidelity-and-variety plan: the LLM-native protocol that turns static figure images into FAITHFUL interactive reconstructions - or honest fallbacks - with fabricated data made structurally impossible. New `references/figure-reconstruction.md` (7 parts): (1) a classification pass over every image block (chart / map / diagram / table-image / photo / screenshot / decorative, recorded into the model's v2 `classification` field); (2) a read-the-figure worksheet template (chart family, axes + units, tick values, legend, per-series readings, stated precision, anomalies) that is embedded as an HTML comment beside every reconstruction so each number is auditable; (3) fidelity cross-checks (endpoints/extrema, category counts, pie/stack sum checks, axis containment, order sanity, unit carry-through) that force a re-read or a confidence downgrade on failure; (4) a three-tier confidence gate - `high`/`medium` build the interactive reconstruction with `provenance: "reconstructed-from-image"`, `confidence`, `source_image`, a provenance badge, and a view-original toggle (`medium` also shows the original alongside with a stated precision caption), `low` ships the enhanced original (pan/zoom lightbox with a one-line reason), NEVER a chart; (5) map/diagram rebuilds allowed only when every label survives; (6) a model round-trip so authoring and coverage reconciliation work from one enriched source of truth; (7) the scanned-page pass - verify every low-confidence OCR block word-by-word, verify ALL numeric content regardless of confidence, transcribe OCR gaps as `provenance: "agent-read"` blocks, and route on-page figures into the classification pass. Wired into SKILL.md as mandatory Instructions Step 3 (pipeline diagram updated, steps renumbered, 3 new rationalization rows, 4 new binary verification items, bundle listing) and into the `/presentify` command's delegation summary. SKILL.md stays at 173 lines.

Validation exercised the protocol for real on the Phase 1 fixtures (agent vision over the extracted images): the deck.pdf vector bar chart classified `chart`, worksheet filled against its rendered ticks, and the reconstruction's values (120/135/150/170, read to the nearest 5) matched fixture ground truth exactly at `medium` confidence; the deliberately-degraded copy (downscaled until ticks are illegible blurs) correctly landed in `low` and shipped as an enhanced original; the unlabeled map classified `map` (SVG-rebuild eligible - zero labels to lose); the photo/logo classified `photo`/`decorative` with a skip entry; and the scanned fixture's OCR was verified against the page images - 3 corrections applied ("QUARTERLYUPDATE" -> "QUARTERLY UPDATE", a merged two-paragraph block split and de-squeezed, "REVENUEFIGURE" -> "REVENUE FIGURE", all re-tagged `agent-read`), the table's 42/37 confirmed against pixels, and page 2's axis-less "illustrative" bar figure was correctly DECLINED for reconstruction (0 fabricated charts). The round-trip enriched models build cleanly (schema v2). Exercising the protocol also exposed a real Phase 1 defect - region crops excluded nearby axis/tick labels, leaving the chart unreadable - fixed inline in `extract_content.py` (`_expand_region_with_labels`: single-pass label-inclusive crop expansion + margin), after which the full Phase 1 verifier re-ran 45/45 green. Validators: bundle audit 0 errors (figure-reconstruction.md referenced from SKILL.md), unicode 0 errors, ruff clean. No registry change (frontmatter untouched; Phase 5 syncs body-size fields); no new outbound call, dependency, or credential.

## [2026-07-11] - v3.12.0 Phase 1: presentify extraction fidelity (PDF visuals, scanned-page OCR, native charts)

Implemented Phase 1 of the presentify-fidelity-and-variety plan (`docs/v3/v3.12/plans/v3.12.0-presentify-fidelity-and-variety.md`): the `document-to-interactive-html` extractor no longer silently drops source visuals. The trigger was a real-world run on a PDF saved from PowerPoint where photos, maps, and figure graphics never reached the output - all traced to deliberate v1 deferrals (DF-v39-presentify-1/-2/-3), now implemented at the extraction layer.

`scripts/extract_content.py` (rewritten, ruff-clean): (1) PDF embedded raster images extract via `pypdf` bytes + `pdfplumber` bboxes, with content-hash dedup of assets repeated on 3+ pages (logos/footers kept once, skipped elsewhere with a `repeated-asset` coverage reason); (2) vector-figure regions (plots/maps/diagrams drawn as vector strokes - the norm in deck exports) are detected by clustering drawing objects into low-text-density bboxes and rasterized at 2x via the new optional `pypdfium2` renderer (`origin: "rasterized-region"`); (3) caption lines directly below a figure attach as the block's `caption` (cue-first "Figure N:" matching, axis-tick-row filter); (4) scanned / image-only pages take a two-tier path - tier A runs a local OCR engine (`rapidocr-onnxruntime` preferred, `pytesseract` accepted) over the rendered page and emits `provenance: "ocr"` paragraph/table blocks with per-block confidence, tier B ALWAYS emits a full-page `origin: "scanned-page"` image block for agent-vision reading, so zero installed OCR engines still means zero content loss; (5) PPTX grouped shapes are recursed (depth-capped) and native PPTX charts extract their real categories/series via `python-pptx` (`provenance: "native-chart"`, chart title as caption); (6) native DOCX chart parts are parsed from the OOXML package with the stdlib (`word/charts/chart*.xml` number/string caches); (7) PDF headings are now typographic (largest-font short line near the top vs the page median) with the first-short-line heuristic as fallback, and a landscape/low-text PDF is tagged `deck_like: true`; (8) a per-source `coverage` manifest counts every visual found/kept/skipped (with reasons) plus scanned/OCR/agent-read pages, so the authoring stage can reconcile - nothing can be dropped silently anymore. Content model bumped to schema_version 2 with ADDITIVE-only fields (documented compatibility rule); `build_presentation.py` accepts v1 and v2. All new libraries stay lazy-imported with `pip install` hints and single aggregated warnings (local-only, zero-network posture unchanged).

Docs: `references/content-model.md` documents every v2 field (image `caption`/`page`/`origin`/`classification`, chart `provenance`/`confidence`/`source_image`/`axis`/`caption`, paragraph/table `provenance`/`ocr_confidence`, source `deck_like`, top-level `coverage`) and the per-format mappings; `references/extraction-runbook.md` rewrites the PDF section (new libraries, two-tier OCR, dedup, deck detection, new gotchas) and moves the formerly-deferred items out of the out-of-scope list. Two one-line truth-fixes were pulled forward from Phase 2 scope (SKILL.md "When NOT to use" bullet and the presentify command's out-of-scope note) so Phase 1 does not ship claims the extractor now contradicts - logged as the phase's only deviation.

Verification: a committed fixture kit (`docs/v3/v3.12/development/fixtures/`, v3.9 worked-example pattern: scripts committed, binaries gitignored) generates five synthetic fixtures - a landscape PDF-from-slides proxy (vector bar chart with ground-truth values, bezier map, photo, 5x repeated logo, captions), a PPTX with a grouped textbox + native chart, a DOCX with an injected native chart part, an xlsx range, and an image-only scanned PDF with known text/table/figure - and `verify_phase1.py` asserts 45 binary checks: all PASS (typographic headings, deck_like, region rasterization + captions, photo extraction, logo dedup, native chart values matching ground truth exactly in both formats, source-data provenance, both scanned pages detected + OCR'd with confidence + full-page images, no-OCR fallback to agent-read pages, no-renderer warning + graceful text/raster continuation, missing-parser pip message, 4-source merge attribution, byte-identical re-extraction including the OCR path, builder v1+v2 compat). Repo validators green (bundle audit 0 errors, unicode 0 errors, version-sync, base parity, compression gate PASSED); ruff check clean on all touched Python. The full pytest sweep's failures (99 bash-invoking hook tests, 4 installer tests, 2 unrelated local tests) reproduce identically on clean HEAD with the phase stashed - pre-existing host/environment issues, recorded as WN-1 in `docs/v3/v3.12/known-gaps.md` with CI authoritative. No registry change (skill frontmatter untouched); no new outbound call or credential; new parser capability is optional, lazy-imported, and installer-neutral (bundle `scripts/` auto-copied).

## [2026-07-10] - v3.11.4: Nexus-AI catalog isolation + docs-layout-refactor universal doc-subtree handling

Shipped v3.11.4, a small catalog patch bundling two independent changes that had accumulated on `develop`. First, the `nexus-ai` integration (`scripts/lib/integrations/nexus_ai.py`) now installs the entire catalog under `~/.nexus-ai/catalog/` (and `<project>/.nexus-ai/catalog/`) instead of the `~/.nexus-ai/` root: the root is reserved for the Nexus-AI app's own data home (settings, MCP config, model weights, session artifacts, credentials vault), so a catalog refresh can wipe-and-refetch its own `catalog/` subtree without any chance of touching irreplaceable app data, and both populators (this installer and Nexus-AI's own syncer) write only under `catalog/`. It also writes a timestamp-free, location-independent `nexus-hub-version.json` at the catalog root recording the installed version (from the single canonical source `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`), the public releases / latest-release endpoints, and a `layout` map of the surface subdirs - a first-class update-detection contract the desktop app polls to prompt the user to update from inside the app, with the manifest's absence signalling "never synced".

Second, the `docs-layout-refactor` skill (1.2.0 -> 1.3.0) gained universal handling for cross-cutting, non-versioned documentation subtrees. The trigger was a downstream plan trying to reshape a project's `docs/adr/` into a `specs/`+`policy/` split with no reference to validate against - a behavior the skill never defined. The fix generalizes: the skill now recognizes a single conservative disposition class covering the widely-adopted documentation standards (append-only decision logs `adr/`/`rfc/`/`proposals/`, architecture/design, the Diataxis quartet, operations `runbooks/`/`playbooks/`, governance/policy/legal, reference collections, and localization), plus a catch-all so an unrecognized-but-comparable subtree defaults into the same class. Every file under a recognized subtree carries a hard floor at Cat 3 (never auto-deleted or auto-archived), is exempt from version-based and whole-major archival, and is never reclassified, split, or renamed by semantic content; a separate rule treats static-site-generator output (`_build/`, `_site/`, `site/`, `public/`, `.docusaurus/`, `dist/`) as regenerable rather than content. This gives `/plan` and `/implement` a canonical rule instead of inventing one. The change is body-only (a new section, Step 4 / Step 5 cross-refs, two worked examples, Edge Cases 11-12); Tier-1 frontmatter and the eight-heuristic model are unchanged, so no `data/` registry update.

Verification: JSON catalogs valid (265 skills), per-skill bundle orphan audit PASS, unicode-safety 0 errors (the edits introduced no non-ASCII punctuation). Release surfaces bumped atomically 3.11.3 -> 3.11.4 across all six version-carrying surfaces (`check_version_sync.py` clean) and the supply-chain manifest regenerated over the release bytes. No catalog count change (265 skills, 16 commands, 25 hooks); no new outbound call, dependency, or credential.

## [2026-07-09] - v3.11.2: Claude Usage Monitor usage-warning sidebar view

Shipped an extension-only patch (Claude Usage Monitor 0.6.0 -> 0.6.1). The usage-threshold warning, prepared for this release as an editor-tab webview panel (`src/warningPanel.ts`), was moved to a compact WebviewView in a dedicated narrow activity-bar container after the panel stole roughly half an editor column. This supersedes both the never-released editor-tab panel and the v3.11.1 notification toast. The move is what actually gives width control: an extension cannot resize an editor group, but it fully controls its own view container (a narrow, user-resizable sidebar).

New `src/warningView.ts` is a `WebviewViewProvider` registered against a `claudeUsageWarning` activity-bar container (`package.json` `contributes.viewsContainers` + `contributes.views`, icon `icons/warning.svg`). Visibility is gated by a `claudeUsage.warningActive` context key: `show()` sets the key true and reveals the view via the auto-generated `<viewId>.focus` command; Cancel/Close post `'cancel'` and `hide()` flips the key false, hiding the view AND its container icon - the genuine "dismiss" a persistent view otherwise lacks. The card is stacked vertically for a narrow column (centered recommendations heading, icon rows for switch-model / reduce-effort, the circular usage ring, a reset box, actions). Buttons are wired with a nonce-gated CSP script and `addEventListener` instead of inline `onclick`, which fixed an unresponsive Cancel. Layout polish per user feedback: lightbulb icon dropped, the recommendations heading doubled to 26px, and the copy tightened to "Ways to extend your usage". `warningPanel.ts` was removed.

The other fix was timeliness ("the warning appears ~10 min late, or only on a manual refresh"). Detection latency is bounded by poll cadence because the usage percent only changes on an API fetch, so `StatusBarManager`'s fixed `setInterval` was replaced with a self-rescheduling `setTimeout` whose delay drops from the configured `refreshInterval` (default 10 min) to ~60s once the active metric is within ~10 points of, or above, the moderate threshold (backoff-aware; guarded so a hide/dispose mid-fetch cannot resurrect the timer). Verification: `tsc -p ./` clean; `vsce package` + install for a visual confirm (the same-version-reinstall gotcha - VS Code only reloads on a version change - was worked around with a throwaway local bump, reset to 0.6.1 for the release). Release surfaces bumped atomically 3.11.1 -> 3.11.2 (`check_version_sync.py` clean) and the supply-chain manifest regenerated. No catalog change (265 skills, 16 commands, 25 hooks); no new outbound call, dependency, or credential.

## [2026-07-08] - v3.11.1: Claude Usage Monitor warning-toast redesign

Shipped an extension-only patch (Claude Usage Monitor 0.5.5 -> 0.6.0) redesigning the usage-threshold warning notification to echo the dashboard's richer look while deliberately staying an auto-dismissing toast. The user supplied a mockup of a full modal-style card (warning header, a 52% usage ring, icon rows for switch-model / reduce-effort / reset, a Cancel button). VS Code extensions cannot render a custom floating modal - the rich card is only achievable as a webview (editor tab / sidebar), which the user declined in favor of keeping the non-intrusive toast. So the work maps the mockup onto what a native notification CAN render: codicons and a progress bar.

Implementation: `buildUsageSuggestion` (recommendations.ts) gained structured fields (`percent`, `label`, `resetsIn`, `switchModel`, `effortAdvice`) derived from the same model-aware logic as the existing prose `message`, so the toast can compose an icon view without re-deriving advice and without drifting from the dashboard (which keeps using `message`). A new `showUsageWarningToast` (extension.ts) renders the warning via `withProgress`: a `$(warning)` title with the metric + percent, then the `$(arrow-swap)` / `$(dashboard)` / `$(watch)` codicon rows for switch-model / reduce-effort / reset-time on SEPARATE lines (newline-joined message), mirroring the mockup's stacked layout. It stays a `withProgress` toast so it self-dismisses on the configured timeout and never stacks (the reason the toast never used `showWarningMessage`), but reports a MESSAGE ONLY - never an `increment` - so the notification's progress bar stays unfilled/absent (the original toast reported no increment either; an earlier draft that reported `increment: percent` added a visible determinate bar, which was reverted on user feedback that the bar was unnecessary).

Verification: `tsc -p ./` clean and `vsce package` produced `claude-usage-monitor-0.6.0.vsix` (27 files). Two runtime behaviors (notification codicon rendering, and whether `withProgress`'s reported message renders `\n` as separate lines) are standard VS Code notification behaviors that could not be exercised in the build environment; the release cut on the maintainer's go-ahead after installing the vsix. Shipped in v3.11.1 (repo bumped 3.11.0 -> 3.11.1 atomically across every version surface; the CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry was promoted to `[3.11.1]` and the supply-chain manifest regenerated). No catalog change (265 skills, 16 commands, 25 hooks); no new outbound call, dependency, or credential.

Shipped v3.11.0, a feature release that turns implicit good practices into command-enforced workflow defaults and bundles four reverse-engineer-first skill-pack adoptions. No `base-*.md` lockstep change was needed: the release is command + skill behavior, not always-loaded instruction text.

Workflow-governance-refinements (the v3.11.0 flagship plan, 8 phases): standardized the per-version docs layout on a canonical `docs/v<MAJOR>/v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>/` scheme (archive at `docs/archive/v<MAJOR>/v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>/`), with a named version-directory-resolution algorithm and release-prefixed artifact filenames; added project-bootstrap governance (`/setup` detects and bootstraps git + a `vX.Y.Z` version + a develop+main branch model + the per-version docs tree; `/describe` and `/review` report a Project-health block with a `/setup` handoff), backed by the reconstituted delegate skills `setup-project`, `analyze-codebase`, and `implement-phase` (which existed only in git history after the v3.2.0 consolidation); made every generated plan end with a mandatory architecture-refactor + known-gaps + CI/CD phase that `/implement` runs on the final phase and `/update release` enforces; upgraded `project-refactor` with empty-dir / duplicate / orphan / structure-complexity detection; hardened `/compare` with a source-security scan and `/presentify` with a render-screenshot-assess visual-QA loop; and made every install verify against each platform's real read-path (a sourced per-platform read-contract table, a Codex/Antigravity delivery fix, project-surface auto-seed, a `nexus-hub doctor` PASS/NEEDS-ACTION report, and a cross-OS CI `install-smoke` job). ## [2026-07-03] - v3.10.1 patch: usage-monitor current-model detection + date-and-time weekly resets

Shipped v3.10.1, an extension-only patch release fixing two user-reported defects in the Claude Usage Monitor VS Code extension (bumped 0.5.2 -> 0.5.3). No catalog change: skills / commands / hooks stay 259 / 16 / 25.

Root cause of the model bug: the dashboard read the current model from the `claudeCode.selectedModel` VS Code setting, which current Claude Code builds no longer write, so `getCurrentModel()` always fell back to `"default"` and the dashboard rendered the hardcoded "Default (Opus 1M)" label regardless of the `/model` selection (verified live: the user's `~/.claude/settings.json` carried `"model": "claude-fable-5[1m]"` while the dashboard said Default). Fix: `getCurrentModel()` now reads the `model` field Claude Code persists to `~/.claude/settings.json`, fresh on every fetch (so both auto-refresh and Refresh Now pick up the latest selection), with the legacy VS Code setting kept as a fallback and `"default"` as the last resort. Display: `formatModelName` now returns only the model family (Fable / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku) -- no "Default" label, no "(1M context)" suffix -- and gains an explicit Fable branch; an undetectable model displays as "Opus" (Claude Code's default tier). Consequence fix: the three model-tier regexes (recommendations, toast notifications, dashboard suggestions) now classify Fable as Opus-class, so a Fable session gets the correct top-tier switch-down advice instead of the low-tier message.

Reset display: `formatResetTime` (and its three mirrors: the dashboard webview's 60-second live-countdown script, the status-bar tooltip prefix logic, and the notification suffix) now renders resets 24h+ away as a concrete date and time plus the remaining duration -- "Tuesday July 7th at 6:59 AM (3 days, 4 hours, 15 mins)" -- instead of the bare "Tue 6:59 AM"; sub-24h countdowns keep the compact "2h 20m" form. The webview live-countdown mirror matters: without it, the 60-second re-render would have clobbered the long-form weekly label back to a raw hour count.

Verification: `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; vsix packaged (`claude-usage-monitor-0.5.3.vsix`) and force-installed (`nexus-hub.claude-usage-monitor@0.5.3` confirmed via `code --list-extensions`). Also committed this cycle (docs-only, rides along in the patch): the v3.11.0 spec-kit third-cycle comparison report (`docs/v3/v3.11/comparisons/v3.11.0-comparison-spec-kit.md`, candidates S1-S8 with the mandatory Security + RE assessment) and its six-phase adoption plan (`docs/v3/v3.11/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md`).

## [2026-06-30] - v3.10.0 adoption-ruflo Phase 5: agent-setup grade + regression diff (re-partial, P2)

Implemented Phase 5 (of 6) of the v3.10.0 `adoption-ruflo` plan: extended `scripts/harness_audit.py` with a single explainable 1-100 agent-setup grade and a cross-snapshot regression diff, surfaced through the `skill-stocktake` skill. Re-partial reverse-engineer build over an owned artifact; strictly local and read-only (stdlib only), zero new outbound call, dependency, or credential. The only write the new code performs is the local grade snapshot under the already-gitignored `.nexus/harness-audit/`.

Model-routing pre-flight: the plan recommends a strong reasoning tier at high effort (Claude Code: Opus 4.8, high) for this phase (real scoring + diff logic that must define a defensible rubric and a stable snapshot format without turning the advisory grade into a hidden gate); the session is on Opus 4.8 (strongest tier), so the re-confirmation agreed and no switch was applied (no-degradation guarantee; live enumeration unavailable in-session, proceeded on the plan recommendation).

Sub-task 5.1 (`scripts/harness_audit.py`, grade capability): added a `grade` action computing a single 1-100 score from six observable, locally-measurable, deterministic signals, each an explainable dimension (name, weight, sub-score, points, one-line reason): `registry_consistency` (0.25 - the registries agree with the on-disk skill count: skills.json `total_skills` + `skills[]` length, SKILL_INDEX.md rows, marketplace.json category sum), `skill_frontmatter` (0.20 - fraction of SKILL.md files carrying all four Tier-1 frontmatter fields), `security_hooks` (0.20 - secret-scan / large-file-guard / git-guardrails present AND registered in settings.json; present-but-unregistered scores half), `instruction_files` (0.15 - the two repo-root surfaces plus the five base-*.md templates present), `hook_registration` (0.10 - every hook command referenced in settings.json resolves to a file on disk, catching orphan references), and `data_integrity` (0.10 - the core data registries parse as valid JSON). Weights live in a single tunable `GRADE_WEIGHTS` constant (mirroring the file's existing `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS` user-contribution slot). The grade is a weighted average over the dimensions that are measurable for the given root (each carries an `applicable` flag and is excluded + renormalized when its inputs are structurally absent), clamped to [1, 100], so a thin install is not penalized for source-tree signals it cannot have. Advisory by contract: prints and exits 0 regardless of score. The repo grades 100/100 (all six dimensions applicable and at 1.00, confirming the 259-skill count is consistent across all registries).

Sub-task 5.2 (`scripts/harness_audit.py`, snapshot + diff): added `snapshot` (writes the graded setup to a deterministic, root-independent JSON baseline at `<target>/.nexus/harness-audit/latest.json`, override via `--snapshot-dir`) and `diff` (recomputes the grade and compares it against the latest snapshot, classifying each dimension improved / unchanged / regressed - added / removed when the dimension set itself changes - plus the overall grade delta). The snapshot payload deliberately excludes the absolute root and any wall-clock field (a separate `snapshot_payload()` from the human-facing `to_dict()`), so two `--snapshot` runs over an unchanged setup serialize byte-identically (verified). Regressions are advisory by default (`diff` exits 0 even when regressed); only `diff --fail-on-regression` opts a CI job into a gate (exit 1 when the overall grade dropped, exit 0 on a first run with no baseline). CLI honors both the positional `grade`/`snapshot`/`diff` actions and `--snapshot`/`--diff` flag aliases; the default no-arg behavior (the existing per-integration `audit`) is unchanged and backward-compatible (the new positional defaults to `audit`).

Sub-task 5.3 (`catalog/skills/workflow/skill-stocktake/SKILL.md`, +12 body lines, now 144): added an "Agent-setup grade (companion signal)" section documenting the `grade` / `snapshot` / `diff` actions as a whole-setup health signal alongside the per-skill quality stocktake, stating plainly they are advisory by default and only gate via `--fail-on-regression`. Cross-links `[[skill-security-scan]]` (per-skill security findings) and `[[skill-eval-loop]]` (per-skill benchmark loop), both added to Related Skills; the plan's optional `[[harness-optimizer]]` was deliberately NOT linked because no such skill exists (it is an agent only), avoiding a dangling wikilink. No frontmatter change, so no `data/` registry edit (v3.8.0 / v3.9.0 refinement precedent).

Stabilization (WN-v33-1: `make` absent on the Windows host, so the documented direct equivalents ran -- ALL GREEN): the four new actions exercised end to end (`grade` -> 100/100 advisory exit 0; `snapshot` -> byte-identical across two runs; `diff` on unchanged -> all-unchanged + zero grade delta + exit 0; `diff --fail-on-regression` -> exit 1 against a strictly-better synthetic baseline, exit 0 with no baseline). ## [2026-06-30] - v3.10.0 adoption-ruflo Phase 4: nexus-hub verify supply-chain command + release manifest (re-full, P1)

Implemented Phase 4 (of 6) of the v3.10.0 `adoption-ruflo` plan: built a local `nexus-hub verify` supply-chain command plus a release-published SHA-256 manifest, the highest-value item in the cycle. Re-full reverse-engineer build over owned artifacts; strictly local (stdlib `hashlib` only), zero new outbound call, dependency, or credential, and no paid code-signing. This phase touches the installer scripts and the release flow (both AGENTS.md "ask first" surfaces), so every change is additive (new copy lines, a new release sub-step) with no refactor of existing copy logic.

Model-routing pre-flight: the plan recommends a strong reasoning tier at high effort (Claude Code: Opus 4.8, high) for this cross-platform installer + release-flow phase (the highest-risk surface in the plan); the session is on Opus 4.8 (strongest tier), so the re-confirmation agreed and no switch was applied (no-degradation guarantee; live enumeration unavailable in-session, proceeded on the plan recommendation).

Sub-task 4.1 (`scripts/generate_manifest.py`, new): a deterministic manifest generator that writes `MANIFEST.sha256` at the repo root in `sha256sum -c` text format (`<sha256><space><space><relative-posix-path>`, LF lines, sorted by path so re-runs are byte-identical). Reuses the existing `scripts/lib/integrations/manifest.py::_hash_path` via the same dual-location import shim as `import_skills.py` (no new hashing code). It owns the single-source-of-truth scope logic the verifier imports: `COVERED_ROOTS` (`catalog/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `data/`), the exclusion predicate (VCS, caches, build, venvs, bytecode, the manifest itself), `iter_catalog_files`, and `parse_manifest`. `extensions/` (the MCP-server sources, pip-installed into a venv) is an intentional, documented out-of-scope boundary (DF-v310-ruflo-P4-extensions in known-gaps). Verified deterministic (byte-identical across two runs, 1100 entries) and `sha256sum -c` clean from the repo root.

Sub-task 4.2 (`scripts/verify_install.py`, new + `scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py`, edited): a read-only, strictly-local verifier that recomputes SHA-256 for each manifest entry against the installed tree and classifies each path OK / MODIFIED / MISSING / EXTRA, printing non-OK entries plus an OK count (Output Minimization) and a single `verify: PASS` / `verify: FAIL (<n> modified, <n> missing, <n> extra)` line, exit 0 on PASS / 1 on FAIL / 2 when no catalog root or manifest is found. The threat-model boundary is the design crux: the catalog root resolves to `~/.nexus-hub/src` (the 1:1 repo mirror the one-line bootstrap materializes, whose layout matches the manifest's repo-relative paths), NOT the bare install root (whose contents are fanned out to per-platform locations) - so verify is honest (exit 2 "no catalog root") on a layout it cannot check rather than emitting false MISSING. Documented plainly in the script docstring and README: a local manifest detects post-install on-disk tampering relative to the published catalog, is trustworthy only to the extent the manifest came from the signed release tag, and is NOT a code signature or a download-channel check. Wired `verify` into the `nexus-hub` CLI core: a lazy-import dispatcher (keeps the network-capable CLI importable without dragging in the verifier, so the existing CLI tests and the only-the-project's-own-GitHub outbound invariant stay intact) plus argv-slice forwarding (argparse.REMAINDER mishandles a leading `--flag`, so `verify` is intercepted before parsing and its args forwarded verbatim). No `.ps1` sibling: both scripts are stdlib-only single `.py` files (NI-v24-1), and the existing `nexus-hub.cmd` launcher already gives Windows parity via the shared CLI core.

Sub-task 4.3 (both installers + release flow): added explicit-name copy lines for `generate_manifest.py` and `verify_install.py` (to `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/`) and `MANIFEST.sha256` (to the install root) in BOTH `scripts/installer.sh` (`safe_copy`, `[OK]` convention) and `scripts/installer.ps1` (`Safe-Copy`, the file's `checkmark` convention), modeled exactly on the `nexus_hub_cli.py` block; the installer's recursive `lib/` copy already lands the manifest hasher beside the new scripts so the installed-layout import resolves. Wired `python scripts/generate_manifest.py` into the `/update release` flow (`catalog/commands/update.md`): a new "release scope: supply-chain manifest" sub-step regenerates and stages the manifest after the version bump (so it hashes the bumped bytes) and before the commit (so it ships inside the release tag and the materialized `~/.nexus-hub/src` tree); the release ordering line now reads `... -> refactor -> manifest, then ... commit, tag, push`. The manifest is a release-time artifact, deliberately not committed during in-progress `develop` work (DF note in known-gaps).

## [2026-06-30] - v3.10.0 adoption-ruflo Phase 2: prompt-injection-defense skill (skill-native, P1)

Implemented Phase 2 (of 6) of the v3.10.0 `adoption-ruflo` plan: shipped a new defensive `prompt-injection-defense` skill, the defender's-seat counterpart to the offensive `ai-attack-patterns`. Skill-native phase -- pure agent-instruction content, no new outbound call, dependency, credential, or third-party processor.

Model-routing pre-flight: the plan recommends a strong reasoning tier at high effort (Claude Code: Opus 4.8, high); the session is on Opus 4.8 (strongest tier), so the re-confirmation agreed and no switch was applied (no-degradation guarantee; live enumeration unavailable in-session, proceeded on the plan recommendation).

Sub-task 2.1 (`catalog/skills/security/prompt-injection-defense/SKILL.md`, 118 lines): a recognition-and-posture skill whose pivot is provenance, not plausibility -- the only sources that may instruct the agent are the user and the system prompt; everything read while doing a task (a fetched page, a file, a tool result, an agent handoff) is untrusted data, never a principal that can issue commands. Teaches the five-part defensive playbook the plan mandates: (1) instruction-origin discipline (imperative grammar in data is not a command); (2) untrusted-content fencing (tag provenance, quote-don't-adopt, never let a block silently escalate privilege or redirect the goal); (3) tool-output skepticism (trust the channel, not the payload; a result asking to run a command, reveal a secret, disable a check, or contact an endpoint is a red flag to surface, not obey); (4) indirect-injection recognition cues (imperative shift, "ignore previous instructions", base64/homoglyph obfuscation, instructions in data fields, exfiltration requests); (5) the safe response (stop, do not perform the side effect, report what + where, hand back to the user). Closes with a defense-in-depth note (sandboxing, least privilege, egress redaction) and states plainly it is posture, not a guarantee. Complements rather than duplicates `ai-attack-patterns`: the offensive methodology (authorization, probes, payloads, Phases 0-7) stays there, and the "When NOT to use" section routes offensive testing and product-architecture defenses away. Cross-links `ai-attack-patterns`, `agent-access-policy`, `egress-redaction`, `advanced-attack-patterns`, plus `security-framework-mapping`. Added an optional `atlas_techniques: [AML.T0051]` mapping with a companion `references/standards.md` (the Phase 1 session history explicitly flagged Phase 2 as the place for it), giving offensive<->defensive symmetry for AML.T0051 in the framework-coverage matrix; D3FEND was intentionally not mapped (no verified countermeasure ID precisely names LLM-prompt-injection defense, and a loose match would overclaim -- recorded in standards.md). Generic naming throughout per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule.

## [2026-06-17] - v3.7.0 install-ux-overhaul Phase 3: `nexus-hub upgrade` checker + CLI on PATH (un-defers N4)

Implemented Phase 3 (of 5) of the v3.7.0 `install-ux-overhaul` plan on `feat/installer-bootstrap`: a `nexus-hub` CLI on PATH whose `upgrade` subcommand compares the installed version against the latest on the project's own GitHub, shows a what's-new summary, and offers an in-place upgrade. This un-defers N4 (DF-v36-1), deferred low-ROI in v3.6.0 and reprioritized as part of the install-UX overhaul.

Model-routing pre-flight: the plan recommends a strong reasoning tier at high effort; the session is on Opus 4.8 (strongest tier) at high effort, so the re-confirmation agreed and no switch was needed.

Architecture decision: a stdlib-only Python CLI core (`scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py`, the NI-v24-1 single-`.py`-no-`.ps1` convention) behind thin native launchers (`scripts/nexus-hub` POSIX, `scripts/nexus-hub.cmd` Windows). Two forces drove it: (a) the core installers already run from any complete tree (Appendix A), so `upgrade` only has to re-invoke the Phase 1 bootstrap rather than add new plumbing; (b) bash cannot be fully run on the Windows dev host (WN-v36-1), and a Python core is directly pytest-able everywhere whereas a pure-shell launcher would be near-untestable locally.

Sub-task 3.1 (CLI on PATH): both installers gained `install_cli_launcher` / `Install-CliLauncher`, called right after templates. Each writes `~/.nexus-hub/VERSION` from the canonical version constant (bash `printf`, PS `Set-Content -Encoding ascii -NoNewline` so no BOM), copies `nexus_hub_cli.py` into `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/` (registered by name in both installers per the installer-aware rule), installs the launcher into `~/.nexus-hub/bin/`, and prints a best-effort PATH hint. The hint NEVER auto-edits a shell rc file / the user's PATH -- a no-prompt install (Phase 2) must not silently mutate the environment; it prints the exact line to add and the direct-run fallback. `--version` reads the VERSION marker (BOM-tolerant via utf-8-sig), with a plugin.json fallback for a standalone tree; the marker is deliberately NOT a `check_version_sync` surface (written from the canonical value, never hand-edited).

Sub-task 3.2 (`upgrade`): reads the installed version, fetches the latest `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` version and the matching `CHANGELOG.md` block from the project's own GitHub (a `fetch_text` helper preferring `curl`, falling back to `wget`, then stdlib `urllib`; a `file://` source is read directly), compares semver numerically (an unparseable installed version sorts as oldest, so it is always offered the upgrade), and prints up-to-date / behind+what's-new. On confirmation it re-runs the Phase 1 bootstrap (`curl|bash` / `irm|iex`); offline / fetch-failure returns a clear message and a non-zero exit with no partial state. A `--yes` flag and a `NEXUS_HUB_UPGRADE_DRY_RUN` seam support non-interactive and test use. Code comments reinforce that the version check is the only new outbound call and it goes to the project's own repo.

Sub-task 3.3 (un-defer N4 + tests): the reverse-engineering matrix gained an "Adopted in v3.7.0" row recording the N4 un-deferral (the upstream `specify self upgrade` named only in the Rationale column per the Attribution Rule), and `docs/v3/v3.6/known-gaps.md` moved DF-v36-1 to Resolved (summary counts updated). `tests/installer/test_upgrade_cli.py` (24 cases) imports the CLI core directly and drives it as a subprocess against a local `file://` fixture via env seams -- covering version reading (file / BOM / plugin.json fallback / unknown), semver comparison, CHANGELOG extraction, the fetch + offline failure, the upgrade subcommand end-to-end (up-to-date / behind+skip / behind+confirmed dry-run / offline), the no-outbound-beyond-GitHub invariant, and both installers' launcher wiring. None of it shells out to bash, so WN-v36-1 does not bite this suite.

Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on this Windows host (WN-v33-1), so gates ran via the documented direct equivalents -- ALL GREEN for the changed code. New `tests/installer/test_upgrade_cli.py` 24/24 passed; `catalog/hooks/tests/test_installer_smoke.py` 51/52 (the lone failure is `test_installer_sh_bash_syntax_clean` invoking WSL `bash.EXE`, which returns 127 on the space-containing checkout path -- WN-v36-1; `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` is independently clean via Git Bash); `tests/validators` 199/200 (the lone failure is the pre-existing `test_session_query_extract.py::test_discover_obsidian_vault_marker`, the same WN-v36-1 WSL-bash-space-path class, untouched by this phase). `shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/installer.sh install.sh scripts/nexus-hub` clean (one SC2088 on an intentional display-only tilde suppressed with a scoped directive + comment); `bash -n` clean on all three; `python -m py_compile scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py` clean; PowerShell AST parse of `installer.ps1` clean; `check_version_sync.py` surfaces all match 3.6.0 (the bump is Phase 5); `validate_unicode_safety.py` 0 errors; bundle-audit / base-template-parity / workflow-security / supply-chain-IOC validators all exit 0. A live smoke confirmed `nexus-hub --version` and `--help`. Quality gate GO. CI (ubuntu) authoritative for the bash path. No new outbound call beyond the project's own GitHub, and no new dependency, credential, or third-party processor.

Pre-existing issues surfaced (NOT fixed -- out of Phase 3 scope, deferred to the Phase 5 release per the Phase 2 note): the `validate_no_personal_paths` gate is red on 3 PRE-EXISTING `C:\Users\<name>` leaks committed in Phase 1/2 docs -- `docs/DEVLOG.md` (the Phase 2 entry that quotes the leak path), `docs/v3/v3.8/comparisons/v3.8.0-comparison-ralph-claude-code.md:265`, and `docs/v3/v3.7/development/history/2026-06-17_install-ux-overhaul-phase-2-no-prompt-install.md:62`. The check was green at v3.6.0 (WN-v33-1 evidence), so this is a v3.7.0 regression introduced before Phase 3; none of the 3 files is in the Phase 3 diff. They should be redacted in Phase 5 (sub-task 5.2) before the release. Next: Phase 4 (interactive guide + docs redesign).

## [2026-06-17] - v3.7.0 install-ux-overhaul Phase 2: no-prompt all-platform install + conflict-only overwrite

Implemented Phase 2 (of 5) of the v3.7.0 `install-ux-overhaul` plan on `feat/installer-bootstrap`: the core installers (`scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`) stop prompting for scope and overwrite, defaulting to a no-prompt global install across all platforms, with a conflict-only overwrite flow that protects user customizations. An AGENTS.md ask-first area, so the one genuine design fork was settled with the maintainer before writing control flow.

Pre-implementation review mapped both installers. Finding: the bash installer had no platform menu (it installed every provider unconditionally) while the PowerShell installer had both a `Select-Platforms` menu and an upfront `Get-Overwrite-Preference` (O/S/A) prompt; instruction files already flow through `merge_marker_section` (structurally safe), so the real conflict surface is the plain `safe_copy` single files (hooks, `mcp-servers.json`, the workspace Copilot file) and the `safe_folder_copy` catalog trees. The diff-based conflict model cannot distinguish a user edit from a Nexus version bump without last-written-hash tracking (which exists only on the Python registry path, not the bash `safe_copy` path), so the maintainer chose **"Diff + refresh-on-yes"** (interactive = one end-of-run prompt naming the files, default keep; `--yes` / `--force` / non-interactive = refresh to latest silently) and **integration keys** as the `--platforms` vocabulary.

Sub-task 2.1 (scope/platform, no prompts): removed the `Select [G/W]` scope prompt and resolved scope from `--workspace <path>` / `-Workspace <path>` (default global). Removed the PowerShell `Select-Platforms` menu and `Get-Overwrite-Preference` prompt, replacing the former with a non-interactive `Resolve-Platforms` that validates a comma list of integration keys (`claude, codex, gemini, antigravity2, gemini-cli, copilot, cursor, opencode, nexus-ai, aider, windsurf, kimi, qwen, openclaw`) into the internal `$platforms` set. Added a bash `should_install <key>` guard wrapping every per-provider block (and the matching legacy-4 permission installs) in both `install_global` and `install_workspace`; the shared instruction-template metadata (PROJECT_NAME/OS_CONTEXT/...) was hoisted out of the Claude block so it is set even when `--platforms` excludes Claude. New flags: `--workspace`/`--platforms`/`--yes`/`--force` (bash) and `-Workspace`/`-Platforms`/`-Yes`/`-Force` (PS), all threaded through the `--branch` re-exec passthrough; a non-TTY stdin (`[ -t 0 ]` / `[Console]::IsInputRedirected`) implies assume-yes so the Phase 1 `curl|bash` / `irm|iex` bootstrap drives a clean no-prompt refresh. The workspace language prompt and the PowerShell terminal `Pause` are both suppressed on the non-interactive path.

Sub-task 2.2 (conflict-only overwrite): `safe_copy` / `Safe-Copy` now compare on-disk content to the source (cmp / Get-FileHash) -- identical files are silent, differing files in refresh mode (`OVERWRITE_ALL=true` / OverwriteMode "ALL") overwrite immediately, and differing files in an interactive run are recorded into parallel conflict arrays and KEPT. A new `resolve_conflicts` / `Resolve-Conflicts` runs once after the install pass: it lists the differing managed files and asks once (default keep; on yes, overwrites the kept set). `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` drop their prompt: refresh mode = full sync (rsync `--delete` / robocopy `/MIR`, removing stale), interactive = non-destructive merge (rsync no-delete / robocopy `/E`, keeping user-added extras). The workspace Copilot instruction file is routed through the unified `safe_copy` path via a temp file (BOM-less UTF-8) instead of its own inline prompt; the bash temp file is cleaned via an EXIT trap, the PS ones after `Resolve-Conflicts`. The `safe_copy` `confirm` parameter is retained for the ~30 call sites' signature compatibility but is now unused (annotated; ShellCheck SC2034-disabled / `$null = $Confirm` in PS).

Sub-task 2.3 (tests): `tests/installer/test_no_prompt_install.py` adds static-surface assertions for both installers (the scope/overwrite/platform prompts are gone, the new flags parse, the conflict accumulators + `resolve_conflicts` / `Resolve-Conflicts` + `Resolve-Platforms` exist, every provider block is platform-gated, refresh-on-yes maps to OverwriteMode "ALL") plus bash-functional tests that extract the four Phase 2 helpers from `installer.sh` and drive them in isolation (fresh-copy/identical-silent/interactive-conflict-collected-and-kept/resolve-yes-overwrites/resolve-no-keeps/refresh-overwrites/folder-full-sync-removes-stale/folder-merge-keeps-extras/should_install-gating) plus the `--platforms bogus` and missing-`--workspace` early-exit-nonzero paths. Three stale `test_installer_smoke.py` guards that asserted the OLD prompt UX (`Select [G/W]`, the Overwrite Request subsection) were inverted to guard the NEW no-prompt behavior. CI already runs `pytest tests/installer` (line 168), so the new file is picked up with no workflow edit.

Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on this Windows host (WN-v33-1), so gates ran via the documented direct equivalents -- ALL GREEN for the changed code. `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` clean; `shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/installer.sh install.sh` clean; PowerShell AST parse of `installer.ps1` clean; `check_version_sync.py` surfaces all match 3.6.0 (the version bump is Phase 5); `validate_unicode_safety.py` reports 0 errors in the changed installers (only the pre-existing checkmark/box-drawing warnings already in `installer.ps1`). Tests: `tests/installer/test_no_prompt_install.py` 8 static passed + 11 bash-functional skipped on Windows (logic separately verified by running the same extract-and-drive harness through Git Bash -- conflict-collected, resolve-yes, refresh-mode, and should_install scenarios all PASS, so they pass on CI ubuntu); `catalog/hooks/tests/` 441 passed + 14 jq-skips (the 3 updated installer-smoke guards green); `tests/installer/` 87 passed (the lone failure is the PRE-EXISTING Phase 1 `test_bootstrap.py::test_ps_standalone_extracts_and_hands_off`, a Windows-host `/usr/bin/tar` extraction issue in the UNMODIFIED bootstrap -- WN-v36-1 class, CI authoritative). `tests/integrations` hangs on this space-containing checkout (WN-v36-1); unmodified by this phase, CI authoritative. Quality gate GO. No new outbound call, dependency, credential, or third-party processor.

Pre-existing issues surfaced (NOT fixed -- out of Phase 2 scope, every changed line traces to the phase): (1) `docs/v3/v3.8/comparisons/v3.8.0-comparison-ralph-claude-code.md:265` contains a `C:\Users\<user>` personal-path leak (committed in `51081c8`, a separate comparison doc) that fails the `validate_no_personal_paths` gate; it should be redacted before the v3.7.0 release (resolved in Phase 5). (2) The diff-based conflict detection can flag a hook that Nexus bumped (not the user) as a conflict on an interactive upgrade -- accepted as the "Diff + refresh-on-yes" tradeoff (the common non-interactive / upgrade path refreshes silently). Next: Phase 3 (`nexus-hub upgrade` checker).

## [2026-06-17] - v3.6.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 3: workflow-phase hook recipe (N1a)

Implemented Phase 3 (of 5) of the v3.6.0 `adoption-spec-kit` plan on `feat/spec-kit-delta-adoption`: the Bucket-B `re-partial` item that gives Nexus-Hub finer-grained workflow-phase automation guidance on its own hook surface (candidate N1a). Built after Phase 4 (the out-of-order build was tracked as NI-v36-1, now resolved). No new outbound call, dependency, credential, or harness event type: the deliverable is a usage pattern over the existing Claude-style hook events plus one advisory example hook.

Pre-implementation review reconciled the plan against the codebase. The plan, comparison, and known-gaps all describe a "4-event model (SessionStart / PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop)", but the live `catalog/hooks/settings.json` template actually registers seven events (it also uses UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, SessionEnd). Those four are nonetheless the events relevant to a workflow *phase* boundary (the other three are session-lifecycle), so the recipe is framed honestly on the four without asserting they are the only events the harness defines, and the pre-existing AGENTS.md "Supported events" line was left untouched (out of scope).

## [2026-06-16] - v3.6.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 2: base-*.md parity-governance check (N3a)

Implemented Phase 2 (of 5) of the v3.6.0 `adoption-spec-kit` plan on `feat/spec-kit-delta-adoption`: the highest-value Bucket-B local re-build -- a repo-internal validator that enforces the AGENTS.md "edit all five `base-*.md` in lockstep" rule structurally, modeled on `check_version_sync.py`. No new outbound call, dependency, credential, or distributed artifact (a repo-internal guard, so no `.ps1` sibling and no installer copy step).

The crux was the structural (not raw-byte) contract. Reading the five templates showed they are NOT structurally identical today, so the plan's suggested "identical heading sets / identical ordered behavioral rules" contract would false-positive immediately: `base-claude.md` is the "full" template (separate Communication Style + Critical Rules sections plus Agent Registry / Spending Controls / Environment Variables / MCP Integration) while the other four collapse those into one Working Conventions section, the AI-attribution bullet wording differs across the four, and `base-gemini.md` omits Context References. Per the plan's "base the contract on what the five actually share", the guard (`scripts/check_base_template_parity.py`) enforces three things: the shared section headings present in all five, the 15 shared placeholder tokens, and the byte-identical bodies of the four invariant sections (Tech Stack, Key Commands, Branching, MCP Registry Policy). The invariant-block check is the core lockstep enforcer and is RELATIVE -- it compares the five files to each other, so an in-lockstep edit to all five passes while an edit to a subset fails, with zero maintenance when shared content legitimately changes. It tolerates the allowed per-platform divergence (platform names, install paths like `.codex/skills/`, the claude-only optional sections, gemini's missing Context References, Output Minimization's claude-only 5th bullet). The guard is scoped to exactly the five lockstep filenames -- it deliberately ignores the 10 later platform-specific `base-*.md` files (aider, windsurf, kimi, qwen, openclaw, antigravity-*, gemini-cli, google-shared). Markdown parsing is code-fence-aware and CRLF-normalized; a missing lockstep file is informational (fewer than two present = clean no-op), so it works on partial trees.

Wiring: added the guard to the Makefile `validate` target (after version-sync) AND -- a real gap the post-phase CI check caught -- to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as an explicit step, because CI's validate job invokes each validator by hand rather than running `make validate` (the same reason `check_version_sync.py` is listed there explicitly). The 9-case pytest module under `tests/validators/` (already run by CI's `pytest tests/validators`) seeds a fixture tree by copying the real templates then mutating one thing: it proves PASS on the real five, FAIL on a removed heading / dropped `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` / reworded MCP-policy block, and -- the false-positive proof the comparison's risk note demanded -- PASS on an allowed per-platform install-path change. AGENTS.md installer-checklist item 4 gained one sentence documenting the machine-enforcement.

Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on this Windows host (WN-v33-1), so gates ran via the documented direct validators -- the validate chain is GREEN (JSON integrity 256 skills, orphan-bundle audit PASS, unicode-safety 0 errors, no-personal-paths exit 0, workflow-security exit 0 confirming the ci.yml edit is clean, version-sync six surfaces match 3.5.0, and the new parity guard exit 0). The 9 parity tests pass. The full repo-level `pytest tests/` reported 494 passed / 4 failed, where all 4 failures are PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: they invoke a bash `.sh` via `bash.EXE` that returns exit 127 because the system bash cannot resolve a script path containing spaces ("OneDrive - Supira"); the scripts exist on disk and the tests pass on the CI ubuntu runner (recorded as WN-v36-1). ## [2026-06-15] - v3.5.0 release: loop-engineering skill enrichment (loopmaxxing + autoresearch adoption)

Shipped v3.5.0, a pure skill-native enrichment of the existing `loop-engineering` skill and its two reference files (`SKILL.md`, `references/loop-schema.md`, `references/loop-library.md`) across three phases on `feat/loop-engineering-enrichment`. No new skill, command, outbound call, dependency, or credential, and no frontmatter change -- so the catalog is unchanged at 256 skills / 15 commands and no `data/` registry edit was needed. The six refinements were distilled from recent loop-design writing and a reference research loop, described generically per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule (a grep for the upstream source names is clean across the skill).

Phase 1 (commit 8ae4ea5) added the strict-control-loop doctrine -- deterministic code drives iteration, execution, and tool/API calls; the LLM is invoked only for the one genuinely-dynamic decision code cannot make, so a hallucinating model's blast radius is bounded by the surrounding hard-coded checks -- plus the progressive-hardening lifecycle that turns an `experimental` loop into a `hardened` one by moving each consistently-correct step out of the prompt and into code (documented in the body and the schema's `maturity` field). Phase 2 (commit 2763890) added the `optimize-metric-keep-best` library archetype (the optimize-a-scalar-metric shape the library lacked: make a change, measure one scalar, keep it only if improved, revert otherwise), the optional `per_iteration_budget` schema field, and the deterministic-oracle carve-out to the maker-self-certifies anti-pattern (one agent may both make and check only when the checker is a non-LLM oracle). Phase 3 (commit f0ade32) added the optional `trace_log`, `progress_check`, and `handoff` schema fields plus a Production Loops note, the concrete two-or-three-retries-then-handoff default in the Scheduled-Triage Recipe, and named "loopmaxxing" in the Common Rationalizations table without weakening any guardrail. With `progress_check` defined in Phase 3, the Phase 2 archetype's forward-references resolve, the central cross-file consistency point confirmed in the final read-through.

Release readiness via `/update release`: `make` is unavailable on this Windows host (WN-v33-1), so gates ran via the documented direct validators -- orphan-bundle audit PASS (both reference files still linked from SKILL.md, no new orphans), quality heuristics PASS, JSON catalog integrity clean, ASCII-only on every edited file, SKILL.md at 131 lines (under the 500-line norm), and the cross-file consistency read-through green. The version bump to 3.5.0 was applied atomically across all six version surfaces (`plugin.json` canonical, `marketplace.json`, both installers, the README and AGENTS.md markers) with `check_version_sync.py` reporting an in-sync tree, the CHANGELOG `## [Unreleased]` block finalized to `## [3.5.0]`, and the README "What's New" rewritten for v3.5.0. No deferred items, so no `docs/v3/v3.5/known-gaps.md` entry was created.

Implemented Phase 3 (of 5) of the v3.4.0 `adoption-nessie-and-agency-agents` plan on `develop`: extended the `session-query` skill's LOCAL discovery and extraction to three additional zero-outbound prior-context sources beyond AI session-log JSONL -- Obsidian vault notes, exported ChatGPT history, and exported Gemini history. `re-full`, local file parsing only: no new outbound call, dependency, credential, or third-party processor.

The design (sub-task 3.1, recorded at `docs/v3/v3.4/development/2026-06-15_session-query-extension-design.md`) keeps the extension additive: the discovery scripts already emit a `tool<TAB>path` tag, so the extractor now uses that tag (or `--tool`/`-Tool`, with extension auto-detect for untagged inputs) to dispatch to a per-source parser, and every parser yields the existing normalized `ts`/`role`/`text` record shape so the topic/branch/time-window filtering, snippet truncation, and `query`/`sessions`/`summary` digest are reused unchanged. JSONL behavior is byte-for-byte identical -- the 13 original extractor tests pass without modification.

Added three parsers to `extract-session.{py,ps1}`: Obsidian (minimal frontmatter scan for a timestamp + title with file-mtime fallback, ATX heading-section split so headings/body/`[[backlinks]]` are all searchable snippets), ChatGPT (`conversations.json` `mapping`/`messages` shapes, epoch `create_time` -> ISO, conversation title prepended to the first message), and Gemini (Google Takeout "My Activity" entries, ISO `time`, title + subtitles/details). Extended `discover-sessions.{sh,ps1}` with Obsidian vault discovery (locate vaults by the `.obsidian/` marker, bounded depth, emit `*.md`, fallback to a plain `*.md` folder) and ChatGPT/Gemini export discovery (default `~/Downloads` canonical-name match; explicit `--root` emits all `*.json`/`*.md`). The new sources are opt-in: the no-`--tool` scan still covers only Claude/Codex/Cursor JSONL, and `--root` without `--tool` still tags `custom` + `*.jsonl`, so default behavior is unchanged and absent sources emit nothing (`test_default_root_scan_ignores_md` asserts this).

One real cross-platform bug was caught and fixed during the parity dry-run: a multi-message ChatGPT fixture returned 0 records in Windows PowerShell while a 1-message fixture worked. Bisection (slicing `Get-ChatgptRecords` out of the script and dumping `$parts`) showed `ConvertFrom-Json` collapses a single-element `content.parts` array to a scalar `String`, which the `$parts -isnot [string]` guard then rejected; Python's `json` never unrolls. The fix makes the `.ps1` parsers accept either a string or an enumerable for `parts`, with the same `@()`-normalization applied to ChatGPT `messages` and Gemini single-entry/`subtitles`; a defensive string-`parts` branch was added to Python for symmetry. Both languages then produced identical digests across all three sources and all filters.

Updated `SKILL.md` (149 lines, ASCII-only): broadened the frontmatter `description`/`summary_l0`/`overview_l1` to name the new sources and add trigger phrases, added a "Sources and default roots" table, new When-to-Use bullets, `--tool` Instructions examples, two Common-Rationalizations rows, and Verification items, keeping the zero-outbound statement explicit. Added a `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry and 13 new cases to `tests/validators/test_session_query_extract.py` (the three parsers, epoch time-window, extension auto-detect, root-scan-with-`--tool`, default-root-ignores-md, stdin tool-tag dispatch, and a bash-gated discovery vault-marker test).

## [2026-06-14] - v3.4.0 model-routing Phase 2: The /route command + switch helpers

Implemented Phase 2 (of 4) of the v3.4.0 `model-routing` plan on `feat/model-routing`: shipped the user-facing standalone half of the feature -- a thin `/route` command and the per-platform `switch-model` helpers that make the confirm-then-auto-execute switch posture real. Skill-native catalog content: no new dependency, credential, remote registry, or third-party processor, and zero new outbound call (the only optional call remains the key-gated Anthropic `GET /v1/models` enumeration in Phase 1's `enumerate-models`).

Created `catalog/commands/route.md` as a thin dispatcher matching the `plan.md` / `implement.md` convention (a pushy SKIP-claused `description` frontmatter for the slash menu; heavy logic stays in the skill). It resolves a TARGET from `$ARGUMENTS` -- a plan phase (`/route phase N of <plan>`), a free-text task (`/route "<task>"`), or the current in-flight task (bare `/route`) -- delegates to the `[[model-routing]]` skill for detection / live enumeration / the complexity assessment, then applies the switch posture per platform tier: execute on scriptable platforms (via the bundled helper), `/model` + `/effort` keystrokes on Claude Code, picker instruction on Cursor / Copilot / OpenCode. A Notes section states it is platform-agnostic and adds zero outbound calls.

Added `catalog/skills/ai-development/model-routing/scripts/switch-model.{sh,ps1}` (stdlib-only, zero outbound, `.sh`/`.ps1` parity, referenced from SKILL.md Step 6 so the orphan-bundle audit stays clean). Contract: `switch-model <platform> <model> [effort]`. On scriptable platforms (Codex / Antigravity `agy` / Gemini CLI) it validates the requested model against the enumerated set before acting -- exact-match against a caller-supplied `NEXUS_ROUTING_MODELS` set (a documented seam that also lets a caller pass a session-cached set to skip re-enumerating), else a substring match against the live `enumerate-models` blob -- then emits the exact non-interactive switch command (`codex -c model=... -c model_reasoning_effort=...`, `agy -m ...`, `gemini --model ...`). Emitting the command (rather than mutating a sibling CLI's live session or silently rewriting a user config file) is the deterministic, idempotent switch artifact. On Claude Code it prints the `/model` + `/effort` keystrokes; on the manual-only platforms it prints the picker instruction. It refuses cleanly: exit 2 (unknown / unrecognized platform), exit 3 (model not in set), exit 4 (set unresolvable -- CLI absent and no `NEXUS_ROUTING_MODELS`). A real bug was caught and fixed during dry-run: the first cut extracted `"id":"..."` JSON fields for validation, but Codex's `codex debug models` output names models under `"slug"` and carries an unrelated `"id":"priority"` service-tier field, so a live `gpt-5.5` failed validation; the fix drops field extraction in favor of the robust raw-blob substring match. A PowerShell parser error (`$effortNote:` read as a scope qualifier) was fixed with `${effortNote}`. Both helpers were then dry-run on this Windows host across bash and PowerShell with identical behavior on all tiers (codex live-enumerated and validated `gpt-5.5` -> emit; `gemini-cli` with no env -> exit 4; `cursor` -> picker; `claude-code` -> keystrokes; unknown -> exit 2).

Bumped the command count 14 -> 15 across the four current-state headline surfaces (README x3, AGENTS.md x2, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `data/marketplace.json`); historical docs left untouched. No skill-registry edit is required for a command, and `/skills list` derives the cheatsheet at runtime, so no static command list was touched. The CHANGELOG `## [Unreleased]` entry records the slash surfaces per the v3.3.4 channels (global on Claude / Codex / Gemini / Cursor / Copilot; project-only on Antigravity 2.0 via `nexus-hub init`; body-only on OpenCode). Added the pytest module `catalog/hooks/tests/test_model_routing_switch.py` (10 cases) covering every switch tier, the model-in-enumerated-set validation contract, the three clean-refusal exit codes, and the `.sh`/`.ps1` parity invariant.

Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on this Windows host (WN-v33-1), so the gate was emulated by invoking the validators, scanner, and pytest directly -- ALL GREEN. JSON integrity (marketplace.json + skills.json load), orphan-bundle audit (RESULT: PASS, 0 warnings -- all four helpers + `switch-model.{sh,ps1}` referenced from SKILL.md), `check_version_sync` (six surfaces match canonical 3.3.4), the v2.3.0 CI validators (no-personal-paths / unicode-safety / supply-chain-iocs / workflow-security all exit 0; every Phase 2 file ASCII- and personal-path-clean), the skill-security scan on `model-routing` (0 findings, install-OK), and the full hook pytest suite (439 passed, 7 pre-existing skips, including the 10 new cases). ShellCheck on `switch-model.sh` was not run locally (not installed) but `bash -n` is clean and CI ShellChecks `catalog/**/*.sh` on the ubuntu runner. All Phase 2 gates passed (GO). Known gaps: DF-v34-1 narrowed (switch helper now pytest-gated; residual is a direct test for `detect-platform`/`enumerate-models`), WN-v33-1 re-confirmed, WN-v33-2 unchanged (recorded in `docs/v3/v3.4/known-gaps.md`). Next: Phase 3 (`/plan` planning-time routing integration).

## [2026-06-09] - v3.2.0 adoption-headroom Phase 4: Runtime integration + retire rtk (nexus-context-compressor)

Implemented Phase 4 (of 7) of the v3.2.0 `adoption-headroom` plan on `feat/adoption-headroom` (switched from `develop`, where the session opened with only stale gitignored `.pyc` artifacts of the compressor and no tracked source -- the Phase 1-3 source lives on the feature branch). Subtasks T012-T015 closed. This phase wires the deterministic engine (Phases 1-3) into a live session and supersedes the external `rtk` recommendation; it is local-first and zero new outbound.

Enabling work (the runtime seam): added `compress_output(text, *, persist=True, store=None, config=None) -> RouteResult` to `__init__.py` -- the single-blob entry both the hook (via the CLI) and the MCP tool call. It runs `ContentRouter`, opens the default CCR store when `persist` so drops stay reversible, and adds two integration-boundary guarantees the raw `route()` lacks: **never expand** (a sub-threshold JSON array that would grow when reserialized is returned verbatim -- a real defect caught in stabilization where `[1,2,3]` went 7 -> 14 tokens) and **never lose output** (a missing/unwritable cache dir degrades to non-persisting compression instead of raising). Rewired `compress(messages)` to route each message's content -- no longer the Phase 1 no-op, resolving DF-v32hr-7 -- and because `route()` no-ops on prose, the all-prose scaffold identity test stays green with `transforms_applied == []`. Added `cli.py` (`compress` reads stdin, `retrieve` resolves a marker, `serve` launches the MCP server; `compress` is fail-open, returning the input unchanged on any error) and repointed `__main__.py` at it while preserving the bare-invocation identity print.

T012 shipped `catalog/hooks/compress-output.sh`, a PreToolUse Bash hook that is opt-in / default-off (inert unless `NEXUS_CONTEXT_COMPRESS=1`, mirroring git-guardrails' protected-branch guard). When enabled, gated on `jq` and on the engine importing cleanly (so output is never piped into a missing compressor), it emits a `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput` rewriting the command to `{ <ORIG> ; } | python -m nexus_context_compressor compress; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` -- piping stdout through the engine while preserving the original exit status (verified end-to-end on both a passing and a failing command) and leaving stderr untouched. Registered in `catalog/hooks/settings.json` (PreToolUse Bash, after the guards) and copied by both installers alongside git-guardrails. Windows uses CLAUDE.md-injected instructions (hooks need a Unix shell), exactly as the prior rtk integration documented. pytest suite at `catalog/hooks/tests/test_compress_output_hook.py` (inert paths run everywhere; rewrite-path tests run with `jq` + an importable engine, skip gracefully otherwise). A first-draft `set -e` + grep-fallback bug (a no-command payload made `grep` exit 1, killing the hook) was fixed by dropping the grep fallback and gating the whole hook on `jq` up front.

T013 added the internal MCP server (`server.py`) exposing `context_compress(payload, persist)` and `context_retrieve(marker)` over stdio, modeled on `nexus-web-fetch`. Unlike that MCP-only package, `mcp` is an optional `[mcp]` extra here and is imported lazily inside `run_server`, so the module -- and its pure `do_compress` / `do_retrieve` handlers + `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS` -- import and test without it (the engine stays usable air-gapped). Registered in `catalog/mcp-configs/mcp-servers.json` (`re-full`, full 5-question audit), with a reverse-engineering matrix row (`docs/policy/mcp-reverse-engineering-matrix.md`, new "New in v3.2.0" section). Both installers now install the compressor with the `[mcp]` extra and auto-register `nexus-context-compressor` (`python -m nexus_context_compressor serve`) in the `mcpServers` merge block -- the installer's own Phase-1 comment had pre-committed this to T013. ShellCheck caught `SC1087` on the install line (`"$dest[mcp]"` is array-subscript syntax to bash) -- fixed to `"${dest}[mcp]"`. Also closed a CI gap: the compressor extension suite was never CI-gated (a Phase 1-3 oversight), so added the install + test step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

T014 rewrote `guides/reference/RTK_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION.md` to lead with the internal engine (no Rust, local-first, reversible) -- platform table, enable/Windows paths, a "Migrating from rtk" section, and the preserved cross-platform output-minimization guidance -- and updated the one rtk reference line in `templates/ai-instructions/base-claude.md`. The supersession is honest about scope rather than overclaiming parity: the deterministic engine compresses **structured** output (JSON arrays, code) today and passes free-text/logs through (the optional Phase 6 ML module), so the guide documents that boundary and leads the reversible CCR store as the real differentiator over (lossy) rtk. The `context-optimization` SKILL.md rtk content is deliberately left for Phase 7's T021 cross-link (DF-v32hr-11).

## [2026-06-09] - v3.2.0 adoption-headroom Phase 1: Foundation + SmartCrusher (nexus-context-compressor)

Implemented Phase 1 (of 7) of the v3.2.0 `adoption-headroom` plan on the new `feat/adoption-headroom` branch (created off the post-teach `develop` merge `8523281`): stood up the internal, local-first `extensions/nexus-context-compressor` package and shipped its first deterministic strategy, `SmartCrusher`. Subtasks T001-T004 closed. This is the reverse-engineer-first internal build that will replace the external `rtk` context-compression binary; Phase 1 is pure standard library plus a single declared dependency (`tiktoken`) that the code never hard-requires at runtime.

T001 scaffolded the package modeled structurally on `extensions/nexus-skill-scanner` (src/ layout, hatchling build, frozen dataclasses, a `tests/conftest.py` that puts `src/` on `sys.path`): `pyproject.toml` (Python 3.10+, `tiktoken` the only required dep, optional `ml`/`code`/`dev` extras), `nexus_context_compressor/__init__.py` exposing `compress(messages, model=...) -> CompressResult` as a Phase-1 no-op pipeline (messages pass through unchanged; metrics report an identity transform), a `types.py` `CompressResult` dataclass (messages + tokens_before/after + `ratio`/`reduction` properties), a `tokens.py` counter that prefers tiktoken's `cl100k_base` proxy and degrades to a deterministic stdlib regex estimate when tiktoken or its cached vocab is unavailable (so the package never requires an outbound call -- the tiktoken vocab fetch is a static asset carrying no user data, mirroring the v3.0.0 OSV.dev / Phase 6 ML-weights offline-first precedent), a `transforms/` subpackage marker, a `__main__.py`, a README, and a scaffold test.

T002 traced the installer distribution mechanism and found the plan's stated assumption wrong: `extensions/` is NOT copied recursively as a folder -- each internal package (`nexus-skill-server`, `nexus-code-search`, `nexus-web-fetch`) has its own explicit `cp -r` + editable `pip install -e` block inside `install_mcp_server`. So the new package would NOT auto-distribute. Per the maintainer's choice (ask-first installer gate), added a matching copy + editable-install block for `nexus-context-compressor` into the shared `mcp-server-venv` in BOTH `scripts/installer.sh` (after the web-fetch block) and `scripts/installer.ps1` (modeled on the web-fetch sibling), with NO MCP-server registration yet -- the compress/retrieve MCP tool is Phase 4 (T013), so the "three internal servers" registration comment is unchanged. `bash -n` + ShellCheck (`-S error`) on installer.sh and a PowerShell tokenizer parse on installer.ps1 are both clean.

T003 implemented `transforms/smart_crusher.py`: a deterministic, dependency-free JSON-array dedup. The load-bearing heuristic, `_distinctiveness_scores`, was chosen after researching how production engines (the headroom source, and Claude Code / Codex compaction) do this -- the key finding being that adjacent-only comparison fails on non-adjacent repetition (`A,B,A,B`), so the score blends GLOBAL uniqueness (content seen anywhere earlier scores 0 -> drop candidate) with ADJACENT change magnitude (a novel record scored by how many fields it changed vs its predecessor, making `variance_threshold=2.0` meaningful as a near-duplicate cutoff). Positional anchors always keep the first and last record; `_select_keep_indices` keeps anchors + records clearing the threshold, capped at `max_items_after_crush` (the cap dominates the positional rule -- the research confirmed headroom's "30%/15%/55%" is a split of the kept budget K, not the array). `_assemble` walks the array emitting kept records interleaved with one `{"_ccr_dropped": "<<ccr:HASH N_rows>>"}` marker per dropped run; the hash is a stable truncated SHA-256 over the canonical (sort_keys) serialization of the dropped span (no randomness/uuid/clock). A `SmartCrusherConfig` dataclass carries the plan's defaults (`min_items_to_analyze=5`, `max_items_after_crush=15`, `variance_threshold=2.0`); a `CrushResult` carries kept records + `CCRSpan` dropped spans (the Phase 2 CCR store's input) + a lossless-accounting `kept_count`. A thin top-level `smart_crusher.py` shim re-exports the strategy and provides the `python -m nexus_context_compressor.smart_crusher` entry the stability gate names verbatim (the implementation lives under `transforms/`, where Phase 3's strategies will also live), resolving a path inconsistency between the gate command and T003's file-location prompt.

T004 wrote 13 SmartCrusher tests (plus 6 scaffold tests, 19 total, all passing) covering every stability-gate assertion -- 1000 identical lines -> 2 kept + 1 marker (<=3); a 12-record high-variance array preserved verbatim; CCR marker hashes stable across runs; `CrushResult` metrics correct -- plus a lossless-accounting invariant (`kept_count + sum(dropped span counts) == original_count`, proving nothing is silently lost), non-adjacent `A,B,A,B` dedup, the budget cap, mixed-type records, determinism, the marker regex format, and the `--demo` CLI. Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on the Windows host, so the gate was emulated by invoking each validator directly -- ALL GREEN. The documented gate command `python -m nexus_context_compressor.smart_crusher --demo` crushes the built-in 100-item array to 5 kept + 4 markers (<=15). `make validate` equivalent green: catalog JSON parses (skills.json unchanged at 251 -- this phase adds an extension, not a skill), `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` PASS, `check_version_sync.py` consistent at canonical 3.1.1 (the new pyproject carries its inception version 3.2.0, which the guard does not scan -- mirroring nexus-skill-scanner's 3.0.0), and unicode-safety / no-personal-paths / supply-chain-iocs / workflow-security all exit 0 with zero warnings in the new package. `make lint` (ShellCheck) WAS applicable this phase (installer edits) and is clean. The new package's `__pycache__`/`.pytest_cache` are already gitignored. No deviations beyond the two plan inconsistencies handled in-flight (installer auto-copy assumption -> explicit block per maintainer choice; gate module path -> top-level shim); all quality gates passed (GO). Known-gaps: 3 new DF (DF-v32hr-1 fuzzy near-duplicate fingerprinting, DF-v32hr-2 information-theoretic auto-sizing, DF-v32hr-3 explicit error/outlier preservation -- all intentionally out of scope for the v1 deterministic port, referenced from the SmartCrusher docstring), 0 resolved; 6 open total (3 DF + the 3 carried-over teach WN). Next: Phase 2 (CCR reversible SQLite store + retrieval interface, so the markers resolve back to originals).
