## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 5: clarification loop + spec quality checklist (`/clarify-spec` command + `spec-quality-checklist.md` template)

Phase 5 of the adoption-spec-kit plan lands the active-clarification surface that pairs with the Phase 4 spec template and the Phase 3 read-only `/analyze-spec` audit. A new `catalog/commands/clarify-spec.md` command implements the sequential 5-question clarification loop with a mandatory Recommended-option contract above every question, a 10-category ambiguity taxonomy (Functional Scope & Behavior, Domain & Data Model, Interaction & UX Flow, Non-Functional Quality Attributes, Integration & External Dependencies, Edge Cases & Failure Handling, Constraints & Tradeoffs, Terminology & Consistency, Completion Signals, Misc / Placeholders), atomic save-per-answer into the spec body plus a `## Clarifications` section, and four distinct stop conditions. A new `catalog/templates/spec-quality-checklist.md` template ships the "unit tests for English" auto-validation surface with Content Quality, Requirement Completeness, and Feature Readiness sections. Three existing artifacts gain body-only updates that wire the new surfaces into the broader SDD workflow: `idea-refine` gains a Boundary subsection clarifying the before-spec vs after-spec division of labor between it and `/clarify-spec`; `spec-driven-development` gains an Auto-validating-the-spec subsection describing the 3-pass checklist iteration plus a new Related Skills cross-link to `/clarify-spec`; `/generate-plan` Step 4 gains a Spec-quality-checklist companion block that writes the checklist alongside the plan when plan type 2 (feature addition) is detected and a sibling `spec.md` exists. This is the G3 + G9 adoption work from [docs/archive/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); like Phases 1, 3, and 4 it ships as skill-native artifacts with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

The new command at `catalog/commands/clarify-spec.md` documents seven steps: resolve the spec file (honors an explicit `<path>` argument, otherwise walks `.specify/feature.json` -> latest `specs/<NNN>-*/spec.md` -> latest `docs/<version>/plans/<slug>.md`, with an explicit abort-with-guidance message when nothing matches), run the structured ambiguity scan across the 10-category taxonomy with each category marked Clear / Partial / Missing, generate the prioritized question queue (at most 5 candidates, balanced across at least 3 distinct categories, ordered by the same `scope > security/privacy > UX > technical` priority that Phase 1 ratified for `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers), the sequential questioning loop with exactly one question per turn (multiple-choice format renders the Recommended option above the table with cited evidence and an aligned-pipes Markdown table of 2-5 options; short-phrase format renders the Recommended <=5-word guess above the prompt; both accept `yes` / `recommended` / `accept` / `r` for the recommendation, a single letter A-E for an option, a free-form short answer for an override, `skip` to defer, and `stop` / `done` / `good` / `no more` to end the loop early), per-answer integration into the spec body (a section-by-section mapping table routes each category to the right subsection -- Functional Scope to FR-### items, Domain & Data Model to Key Entities, Interaction & UX Flow to Acceptance Scenarios, Non-Functional Quality Attributes to measurable thresholds, Integration to External Dependencies, Edge Cases to the eponymous subsection, Constraints to the header or a Constraints subsection, Terminology to canonical-name replacement across all sections, Completion Signals to SC-### items, Misc / Placeholders to in-place replacement) followed by an atomic save (temp file + fsync + rename) and a one-line confirmation echo, the four stop conditions (5 questions asked, all critical ambiguities resolved with no Missing categories and at most one Partial, user signal, empty queueable set), and the completion report with the per-category before/after status table, outstanding-ambiguities bullets, and a recommended-next-command branch. The command exposes three invocation forms: `/clarify-spec` (default, latest spec), `/clarify-spec <path>` (explicit spec file or feature directory), and `/clarify-spec --max-questions N` (lower the question cap; never raise above 5). The behavior guarantees are explicit: sequential questioning (never two questions in one message), Recommended-option mandatory with cited evidence, atomic save per answer (a crash mid-loop leaves the spec consistent up to the last answered question), hard cap 5 questions, no new sibling files created (`clarifications.md` / `q-and-a.md` are explicitly disallowed -- the loop only edits the spec in place and adds the `## Clarifications` section), and cross-link discipline (FR-### / SC-### IDs added or modified during the session remain stable, with new IDs using the next sequential number in the spec's existing scheme).

The new template at `catalog/templates/spec-quality-checklist.md` ships with three checklist sections: Content Quality (no implementation details, focused on user value, written for non-technical stakeholders, all mandatory sections completed), Requirement Completeness (no `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers remain, requirements are testable and unambiguous, success criteria are measurable and technology-agnostic, all acceptance scenarios defined, edge cases identified, scope clearly bounded, dependencies and assumptions identified), and Feature Readiness (every functional requirement has clear acceptance criteria, user scenarios cover primary flows, the feature meets measurable outcomes from Success Criteria, no implementation details leak into the spec). The closing Notes section codifies the iteration contract: items that remain unchecked after 3 passes must be documented in the spec's `## Assumptions` section before advancing to `/clarify-spec` or `/generate-plan`; FR-### or SC-### IDs that are inherently non-testable must be rewritten rather than silently ticked; the checklist validates the spec's prose ("unit tests for English") rather than implementation correctness (which is validated separately by tests against FR-### / SC-### IDs via `[[cross-artifact-analyzer]]`'s coverage matrix).

Three existing artifacts gain body-only updates. `catalog/skills/developer-experience/idea-refine/SKILL.md` Step 5 (Identify Open Questions) gains a new `Boundary with /clarify-spec` paragraph immediately after the existing 3-marker-cap paragraph, clarifying that `idea-refine` operates BEFORE a spec exists (input: a vague idea or `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`-laden problem statement; output: a one-page problem statement with bounded scope and observable success criteria) while `/clarify-spec` operates AFTER `spec.md` is written (input: a structured spec with FR-### / SC-### IDs; output: the same spec with ambiguities resolved at the requirement and user-story granularity through the sequential 5-question loop). The paragraph explicitly notes that `/clarify-spec` should not be invoked against a vague problem statement -- it expects the structured template from `catalog/templates/spec-template.md`. `catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` gains a new `### Auto-validating the spec` subsection immediately after the `### User stories with priorities` subsection from Phase 4, documenting the 3-pass iteration (Pass 1 Content Quality, Pass 2 Requirement Completeness, Pass 3 Feature Readiness) and the post-3-pass behavior (remaining unchecked items go into `## Assumptions` and warn the user before advancing). The same skill body gains a new Related Skills cross-link to `/clarify-spec` describing it as the Phase 5 sequential 5-question loop that resolves spec ambiguities after the template's slots are filled and pairs with the spec-quality-checklist for the final readiness gate before `/generate-plan`. `catalog/commands/generate-plan.md` Step 4 gains a new `### Spec-quality-checklist companion (feature-level plans only)` block immediately after the existing Constitution Check + Complexity Tracking discussion that resolves the target directory (`docs/<version>/plans/<slug>/checklists/requirements.md` for the default layout or `specs/<NNN>-<slug>/checklists/requirements.md` for the Phase-7 opt-in layout), copies the template with `[FEATURE NAME]` / `[DATE]` / `[Link to spec.md]` placeholders replaced, leaves an existing checklist file in place (with an announcement directing the user to rerun `/clarify-spec` or edit the checklist directly to refresh), and tells the user the next step (run `/clarify-spec` if unchecked items remain, or `/analyze-spec` followed by `/implement-phase <slug> phase-1` if all items pass). The block explicitly skips the checklist companion for plan types 1 (initial greenfield build), 3 (refactor), and 4 (other) since none of those plan types produces a feature spec; the Constitution Check section above is still emitted for all plan types.

Phase 5 does not introduce a new skill -- it ships one new command, one new template, and three existing-artifact body updates -- so no `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, or `data/marketplace.json` updates are required. The template lives under `catalog/templates/` which is already auto-copied by the installer's `install_templates` block (via `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy`) to `~/.nexus-hub/templates/`; commands under `catalog/commands/` are already auto-copied to each platform's command directory (Claude `commands/`, Codex `prompts/`, Gemini `workflows/`) via the same recursive primitive. No installer edit is required.

Validation runs clean: JSON parse on all five `data/*.json` files succeeds with UTF-8 encoding (`skills.json` still reports 205 entries -- unchanged from Phase 4 close); the skill-bundle audit (`python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only`) returns 0 errors and 0 warnings across the 209 skills it scans (no orphan bundles introduced because Phase 5 ships only a top-level command, a top-level template, and three existing-artifact body edits; no new bundled `scripts/`, `references/`, or `assets/` subdirectories). The full-validator pass on the two updated skill files returns 0 errors and 5 pre-existing baseline warnings each (missing optional `author` / `version` / `category` / `license` / `tags` frontmatter fields -- identical to the warning profile that was present before Phase 5 and matches the established baseline across the catalog). ## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 4: spec template upgrade (`catalog/templates/spec-template.md` + `spec-driven-development` skill updates)

Phase 4 of the adoption-spec-kit plan lands the canonical spec template that downstream tooling keys off and the `spec-driven-development` skill body that enforces it. A new `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` ships with the eight mandatory sections in order -- Header block, User Scenarios & Testing (with prioritized P1/P2/P3 user stories carrying Independent Test paragraphs and Given/When/Then Acceptance Scenarios), Edge Cases, Requirements (with `**FR-###**: System MUST <capability>` IDs and an optional Key Entities subsection), Success Criteria (with `**SC-###**: <measurable outcome>` IDs), and Assumptions. The `catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` body gains two new subsections (Spec template; User stories with priorities), two new Common Rationalizations rebuttals (bullet-points-vs-IDs; single-user-story specs), and two new Related Skills cross-links (`cross-artifact-analyzer`, `project-constitution`). This is part of the Bucket A skill-native adoption work from [docs/archive/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); like Phases 1 and 3 it ships with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

The new template at `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` is the surface every feature spec is meant to start from. The opening HTML comment block documents the section conventions (mandatory MUST be completed; optional include-if-relevant; remove entirely when not applicable -- do not leave as "N/A"), the `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: <specific question>]` marker rules with the Phase 1 hard cap of 3 markers per spec prioritized by `scope > security/privacy > UX > technical`, and the FR-### / SC-### ID convention that `/analyze-spec` consumes. The User Scenarios block guides authors toward prioritized journeys (P1 = smallest scope that delivers user value; P2 / P3 add value but are not required for the MVP), each with a `**Why this priority**` justification, an `**Independent Test**` paragraph (the smallest end-to-end check that proves the story is delivered, runnable without implementing any other story), and Given/When/Then Acceptance Scenarios. The Requirements block uses `**FR-001**: System MUST <capability>` with FR-002 carrying an example `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker so the template surfaces the convention without forcing the user to remember it. The Success Criteria block uses `**SC-001**: <measurable outcome>` with HTML-comment guidance listing the four criteria (Measurable, Technology-agnostic, User-focused, Verifiable) and the anti-patterns to avoid (`"System is fast"`, `"Uses Redis for caching"`, `"Code is well-structured"`, `"Tests pass"`). The Assumptions section is mandatory whenever any candidate ambiguity was demoted below the 3-marker hard limit from Phase 1.

The `spec-driven-development` skill body gains the new "Spec template" subsection immediately after the `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker convention. The subsection explains why the FR-### / SC-### IDs matter (they are the join key the `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill uses to build the Coverage Summary table in `/analyze-spec`; a spec written with prose bullets instead of IDs produces an empty matrix and the analyzer cannot flag missing tasks) and documents the three ID-stability rules: sequential within category (FR-001, FR-002, ...; SC-001, SC-002, ...), stable across edits (once assigned, do not renumber; removing a requirement leaves a gap), and unique within the spec but not globally across the project (FR-001 in two different specs are different requirements). The new "User stories with priorities" subsection enforces the three disciplines downstream tooling depends on: priority labels P1/P2/P3 assigned by user value rather than implementation order (with the explicit note that the Phase 6 `[US#]` task label is keyed off these IDs); the Independent Test paragraph that proves each story is deliverable in isolation (the MVP contract: implementing only P1 must pass the P1 Independent Test even when P2 and P3 are untouched); and the MVP rule that implementing just P1 must deliver value to a real user, with the example anti-pattern of a P1 story like "set up the database schema" -- an enabler, not a user story. The subsection also handles the single-story case explicitly: still use `### User Story 1 - [Title] (Priority: P1)` with the full Independent Test and Acceptance Scenarios so `/analyze-spec` can find the story regardless of count.

Two new Common Rationalizations rebuttals join the existing five-row table: "I'll just use bullet points instead of FR/SC IDs" rebuts with the failure mode (the IDs are not decoration; they are the analyzer's join key; an empty matrix means missing tasks cannot be flagged) and points at the template; "This feature only has one user story" rebuts by explaining the single-story case explicitly (still write it as User Story 1 with priority P1 plus the Independent Test paragraph and Acceptance Scenarios because `/analyze-spec` and the Phase 6 task discipline both find the story by its heading regardless of count). ## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 3: cross-artifact spec analyzer (`/analyze-spec` + `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill)

Phase 3 of the adoption-spec-kit plan lands the read-only cross-artifact consistency analyzer: a new `/analyze-spec` command at `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` and its companion `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill at `catalog/skills/code-review/cross-artifact-analyzer/SKILL.md`. The analyzer reads a feature directory's spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md (plus the project constitution from Phase 1 if it exists at `docs/<version>/constitution.md`), runs six detection passes (Duplication, Ambiguity, Underspecification, Constitution Alignment, Coverage Gaps, Inconsistency), assigns severity per a documented heuristic (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW), and emits a Markdown report with three tables (Findings capped at 50 rows with overflow summary; Coverage Summary keyed by FR-### / SC-###; Metrics block) plus Next Actions. This is the G4 adoption candidate from [docs/archive/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); it ships as a skill-native artifact with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

As part of this phase, the source plan file was relocated from `docs/archive/v2/v2.0/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md` to `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md` to align with the targeted release version. The Plan and Plan reference links inside `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` were updated to point at the new location.

The new command at `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` documents seven steps: resolve the feature directory (honors an explicit `<path>` argument, otherwise walks `.specify/feature.json` -> latest `specs/<NNN>-*/` -> latest `docs/<version>/plans/<slug>.md`); load minimal context per artifact (only the sections each detection pass needs, with a self-contained-plan fallback that parses functional requirements out of phase prompts, success criteria out of Stability Gate text, and tasks out of `- [ ] T###` lines); run the six detection passes in order; assign severity per the heuristic with promotion allowed and demotion not allowed; assign deterministic category-prefixed IDs (`A1, D1, U1, C1, G1, I1`) sorted within a category by source-line number; emit the report; report completion. The command exposes three invocation forms: `/analyze-spec` (default, latest feature), `/analyze-spec <path>` (explicit directory or plan file), and `/analyze-spec --output <path>` (write the report to a file in addition to stdout). The behavior guarantees are explicit: read-only (the only writable target is the optional `--output` path), deterministic IDs across reruns, constitution-aware-but-optional (Pass 4 emits an informational N/A when the constitution file is absent), overflow-safe (Findings table is capped at 50 rows with a one-line summary pointing at `--verbose` for the full list). The command body ends with a mandatory closing statement -- "This analyzer is read-only. It modifies no files. Any remediation requires user approval." -- that the report MUST also emit regardless of how it was rendered.

The new skill at `catalog/skills/code-review/cross-artifact-analyzer/SKILL.md` drives the command end-to-end. Required YAML frontmatter is complete (`name`, `description`, `summary_l0`, `overview_l1`), the description follows the pushy-description rule from `AGENTS.md` with trigger phrases verbatim ("analyze the spec", "is this spec ready", "do all requirements have tasks", "coverage check", "ambiguity check", "spec-plan-tasks consistency", "cross-artifact analysis", "constitution alignment check on this plan", "find gaps in this feature") plus a SKIP clause that fences off full code-review of an implementation, single-file lint passes, runtime profiling, and test execution. The body covers all required sections (When to Use, Inputs table, Instructions, Common Rationalizations, Verification, Related Skills). The Rationalizations table rebuts six excuses the agent might use to skip the analyzer ("too small a feature", "/generate-plan already cross-checks", "I'll read it myself", "constitution alignment will always pass", "I'll just delete findings I disagree with", "IDs will change on rerun anyway"). Cross-links via `[[name]]` syntax point to `project-constitution` (source of MUST principles for Pass 4), `ambiguity-detector` (shares the vague-adjective and [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] detection logic; this analyzer applies it cross-artifact while ambiguity-detector operates per-text), `spec-driven-development` (defines FR-### / SC-### / user-story-priority conventions), `implementation-plan` (produces the plans this analyzer audits), `idea-refine`, `known-gaps-tracker`, and `final-report` (sibling code-review skill; this analyzer focuses on specification artifacts while final-report consolidates findings from a full code review).

The three data registries are updated per the rule in `AGENTS.md`: `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gains a new row for `cross-artifact-analyzer` and bumps the total from 204 to 205; `data/skills.json` gains a new entry following the established schema; `data/marketplace.json` bumps the code-review category `skill_count` from 9 to 10. The pre-existing `data/skills.json` statistics drift (WN-1, opened in Phase 1) is now compounded by one more entry -- the skills array length reads 205 while `statistics.total_skills` still reads 197 -- and the WN-1 entry in `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` was updated to record that compounded value. The drift remains scheduled for repair via `make build-catalog` in Phase 8 sub-task 8.1 step 5.

Validation runs clean: JSON parse on all five `data/*.json` files succeeds with UTF-8 encoding; the skill-bundle audit (`python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only`) returns 0 errors and 0 warnings across the 209 skills it scans (208 in Phase 1; +1 for the new cross-artifact-analyzer); the full-validator pass on the new skill returns 0 errors with 5 baseline warnings (missing optional `author` / `version` / `category` / `license` / `tags` frontmatter fields -- identical to the warning profile of the sibling `project-constitution` skill, confirming the new skill matches the established baseline). Phase 3 introduced no DEVIATION markers, no test failures, no suppressed lint rules, and no bypassed gates; `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` records a Phase-3-close note with no new items added and no items resolved.

Next: Phase 4 -- spec template upgrade. `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` will land with mandatory User Scenarios (P1 / P2 / P3 user stories each with Independent Test criteria), Functional Requirements as FR-### entries, Success Criteria as SC-### entries, and Key Entities subsections. The `spec-driven-development` skill will gain new subsections enforcing the template and the user-story discipline, and Common Rationalizations rebuttals for "bullet points instead of IDs" and "this feature only has one user story". ## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 1: project constitution + NEEDS CLARIFICATION marker discipline

Phase 1 of the adoption-spec-kit plan ([docs/archive/v2/v2.0/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md)) lands the foundation that downstream phases depend on: a new `project-constitution` skill, a new `/constitution` command, a new `catalog/templates/constitution-template.md` skeleton, and a standardized `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: <specific question>]` marker convention (with a hard cap of 3 markers per artifact and a fixed priority order `scope > security/privacy > UX > technical`) wired into three existing developer-experience skills. This is the Bucket A / G1 + G2 work from [docs/archive/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); both adoption candidates ship as skill-native artifacts with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

The new skill at `catalog/skills/workflow/project-constitution/SKILL.md` defines the constitution as a versioned project-governance file (MUST / SHOULD principles that bind every plan, spec, ADR, code review, and release) distinct from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (which are agent-instructions for AI tools). The body covers file location (recommended: `docs/<version>/constitution.md`; acceptable: `CONSTITUTION.md` at root), the required structure (preamble, numbered principles with Statement / Rationale / Applies to subsections, governance, versioning), the amendment workflow (SemVer applied to principles: MAJOR for removals or redefinitions, MINOR for additions, PATCH for clarifications), the Sync Impact Report HTML comment emitted at the top of the file on every edit (version change, modified principles, added or removed sections, templates and commands requiring updates), and the Constitution Check gate that Phase 2 wires into `/generate-plan`. The frontmatter description follows the pushy-description rule from `AGENTS.md` -- trigger phrases verbatim plus a SKIP clause covering CLAUDE.md edits, single-feature READMEs, one-decision ADRs, and commit-message conventions. The skill cross-links via `[[name]]` syntax to `spec-driven-development`, `architecture-decision-record`, `implementation-plan`, `ambiguity-detector`, `idea-refine`, and `known-gaps-tracker`.

The new command at `catalog/commands/constitution.md` drives the skill end-to-end with a seven-step flow: resolve constitution location (detects existing files at `docs/<version>/constitution.md`, older `docs/v*/constitution.md`, or `CONSTITUTION.md` at root and picks the most recent), collect or derive placeholder values (interactive question loop in author mode; targeted edit prompts in amend mode), draft the constitution content from the template, run the propagation check across `catalog/commands/generate-plan.md`, `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` (when Phase 4 ships it), `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` (when Phase 3 ships it), and any plan or ADR that cites the constitution, emit the Sync Impact Report, validate (header completeness, ISO dates, no leftover `[ALL_CAPS_IDENTIFIER]` placeholders, principle-subsection completeness, 3-marker cap, version-increment matches change classification), and write. The command uses Nexus-Hub-native framing throughout per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule -- no upstream attribution leaks into the user-facing artifact. A `/constitution check <plan-path>` shorthand runs the Constitution Check gate read-only against an existing plan or spec.

The new template at `catalog/templates/constitution-template.md` is a skeleton with placeholder slots for the Sync Impact Report HTML comment, the four header fields (Project, Version, Ratified, Last Amended), the Preamble, three principle subsections each with Statement / Rationale / Applies to (extensible up to 7), two optional sections (Operational Standards, Quality Bars), Governance, and Versioning. Placeholders are bracketed with `[ALL_CAPS_IDENTIFIER]` so the validator in the `/constitution` command can detect any that were not filled in.

The three existing developer-experience skills get a new subsection each that aligns them with the marker convention: `spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` gains "Marking uncertainty with `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`" under "When to Use This Skill", with rules, examples, and the 3-marker cap; `ambiguity-detector/SKILL.md` gains "Step 7: Emit `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` Markers Aligned with the Project Convention" after Step 6 (Generate the Ambiguity Report), explaining how the detector's output flows back into the spec text using the standardized marker rather than free-form prose; `idea-refine/SKILL.md` gains a paragraph under "Step 5: Identify Open Questions" cross-linking to the convention and clarifying that the refinement of vague ideas should produce no more than 3 outstanding markers, with the rest resolved via informed defaults. All three updates cite the priority order verbatim ("scope > security/privacy > UX > technical"), include the hard limit ("Maximum 3 markers total"), and use the `[[name]]` link syntax to cross-link the four skills (the three existing + the new `project-constitution`).

The three data registries are updated per the rule in `AGENTS.md`: `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gains a new row for `project-constitution` and bumps the total from 203 to 204; `data/skills.json` gains a new entry and bumps `statistics.total_skills` from 196 to 197 and the workflow category count from 19 to 20 (note: these statistics fields had been pre-existingly out of sync with the actual skills array length -- the array now holds 204 entries while the statistics block reads 197, mirroring a drift that has been present since before v2.0.0; the discrepancy is tracked in `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` as WN-1 for Phase 8 release stabilization to repair via `make build-catalog`); `data/marketplace.json` bumps the workflow category `skill_count` from 21 to 22 and updates the category description to mention "project governance".

Validation runs clean: the skill-bundle audit (`python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only`) returns 0 errors and 0 warnings across the 208 skills it scans; the full-validator pass on the new skill returns 0 errors with 5 baseline warnings (missing optional `author` / `version` / `category` / `license` / `tags` frontmatter fields -- identical to the warning profile of the sibling `known-gaps-tracker` skill, confirming the new skill matches the established baseline); the three updated existing skills each return 0 errors with the same 5 baseline warnings (no new warnings introduced by the body edits); all five JSON files in `data/` parse cleanly with UTF-8 encoding. An end-to-end constitution document was authored at `scratch/constitution-test.md` to verify the template + command flow produces a structurally-correct file (Sync Impact Report HTML comment at the top, all four header fields present, ISO dates, no leftover placeholders, all three principle subsections present per principle, Governance and Versioning sections present), and the scratch file was deleted after the check passed.

The known-gaps file for v2.1.0 is created at `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` (status `in-progress`) with the single WN-1 entry documenting the pre-existing `data/skills.json` statistics drift. v2.0.0 known-gaps remains finalized; this Phase 1 work does not reopen it.

Next: Phase 2 -- wire the constitution from Phase 1 into the plan-generation workflow as a Constitution Check gate. `/generate-plan` will gain a Constitution Check section near the top of the produced plan (PASS / FAIL / N/A per MUST principle with a one-sentence justification, or the informational "no constitution file found" note when the file does not exist) and a Complexity Tracking table near the end (filled only if Constitution Check has violations that must be justified). Both lead with the rename as the breaking change, then walk through the six subsections (Renamed / Breaking changes / Added / Changed / Migration / Carry-overs) per the plan's structure. Pass 2 was triggered by the post-sweep audit grep, which surfaced 7 files still carrying the MCP-server key tokens (`devai-skill-server`, `devai-code-search`, `devai-web-fetch`) plus the pre-commit `.git/hooks/pre-commit.devai-backup-<timestamp>` pattern that variants 1-6 did not cover. Adding variants 7-14 (the MCP keys, the snake-case Python package ids, `devai_mcp_benchmark`, and `devai-backup`) and re-running the script touched a further 7 files with 32 replacements. Combined: 66 unique files, ~209 replacements, ~195 changed lines. The script is idempotent and writes a per-file manifest to `docs/archive/v2/v2.0/rename-manifest.txt` for traceability. It is allowlisted as a developer-only utility in `catalog/hooks/tests/test_installer_smoke.py` via `DEV_ONLY_SCRIPTS`, so the regression test that enforces "every `scripts/*.py` is in both installers" does not block the maintainer tool from landing.

`scripts/Install-DevAI-Permissions.ps1` -> `scripts/Install-Nexus-Hub-Permissions.ps1` is the only Phase 4 sub-task 4.3 work that remained after the Phase 3 pull-forward of `scripts/devai_mcp_benchmark.py`. ## [2026-05-19] - v1.3.0 adoption-pm-claude-skills Phase 5: marketing pattern adoption (README roadmap and narrative DEVLOG entry)

The `adoption-pm-claude-skills` arc started with `/compare-project` pointed at [`mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills`](https://github.com/mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills). The comparison report ([docs/archive/v1/v1.3/comparison-pm-claude-skills.md](v1.3.0/comparison-pm-claude-skills.md)) classified the upstream catalog into 9 in-scope adoptions and 5 explicit drops. The 9 adoptions split cleanly along the MCP Registry Policy decision tree: 8 went into the `skill-native` bucket (zero code, zero outbound calls, ship as SKILL.md files), 1 was a `re-full` bundle expansion, 0 needed `re-partial` work, and 0 qualified for the trusted-vendor wrapper tier.

The adoption philosophy was straightforward: skill-native first per the [MCP Registry Policy](../AGENTS.md) decision tree. The 6 engineering document-template skills shipped in Phases 2 and 3 (`incident-postmortem`, `runbook-writer`, `oncall-runbook`, `pr-description-writer`, `architecture-decision-record`, `test-strategy-doc`) close the "advisor vs. document-producer" gap that the upstream catalog exposed. DevAI-Hub already had advisor skills like `sre-engineer`, `code-quality`, and `intent-based-review` that conceptually covered postmortems, runbooks, on-call procedures, and PR review. What was missing was a dedicated artifact-producing skill for each. Phase 4 then bundled the new and existing skills into three one-click groupings: `incident-response`, `pr-workflow`, and `architecture-docs`.

Five upstream items were dropped explicitly and recorded in the plan's out-of-scope appendix. The 4-template vendor-connector pattern (`pm-sprint-agent`, `pm-discovery-agent`, `pm-stakeholder-comms-agent`, `pm-launch-agent`) violates the registry policy's hard-no list because each template bundles MCP wrappers for vendor SaaS that DevAI-Hub categorically rejects ("search-as-service, embeddings-as-service, scraping-as-service, generation-as-service"). The flat `skills/<name>/` directory layout is a structural regression versus the 22-category nested layout that `make validate`, the registry generators, and `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` schema all depend on. The ~108 non-engineering skills (PM / Marketing / Legal / Finance / HR / Sales / Operations / Design-UX / Healthcare-Research / Cross-Profession / Figma) are out of scope per the AGENTS.md repository overview that pins DevAI-Hub as a coding-assistant catalog. The `system-design-interview` skill is also out of that scope. Sponsor-tier README framing is out of scope per the company-neutral, personal-project stance.

One cross-cutting note worth flagging: the cumulative cross-OS installer smoke run from the v1.1.5 known-gaps cluster (DF-003 / DF-005 / DF-006 / DF-007 / DF-008 / QG-001) remains the durable fix for installer smoke coverage and is NOT extended by this adoption. Every artifact shipped through Phases 2 to 5 is a pure SKILL.md file or a Markdown edit. No new repo-level scripts, no new bundled subdirs, no installer-aware copy lines. The cluster carries forward unchanged to v1.5.0+ as a separate cross-cutting CI track. The plan ([docs/archive/v1/v1.3/plans/adoption-pm-claude-skills.md](v1.3.0/plans/adoption-pm-claude-skills.md)) targets v1.4.0 as the release; Phase 6 will compose the CHANGELOG `[1.4.0]` block, confirm cumulative validators are green, and hand off to `/wrap-up-session` for the version bump.

## [2026-05-12] - Cross-surface description format: single-line `# Description:` prefix replaces the 4-line box

*   **Goal**: Make the description that DevAI-Hub injects into shell-tool approval dialogs render legibly on every agentic surface, not just the VS Code Claude Code extension and the Claude Code terminal. The four-line `# ===== Description ===== #` box that v1.1.0 introduced renders beautifully on surfaces that unescape `\n` (VS Code extension, terminal), but on surfaces that show the tool input as raw JSON (notably the Claude Desktop app, screenshotted by the user) the same `\n` characters become literal escape text and the box turns into unreadable noise. The fix needs to be universal: a single format that degrades gracefully on every surface without relying on any specific JSON-rendering behavior.

*   **Diagnosis**: The `description` field is the only output channel that **every** approval-dialog surface renders cleanly (as a subtitle line under the command). The `command` field is shown by every surface, but its `\n` rendering varies. The `permissionDecisionReason` field is newer Claude Code surface-only. The previous hook design leaned on the `command` field's `\n` rendering for the description, which is the channel with the widest cross-surface variance. The right architecture is to lean on the `description` field (universal channel) and degrade the `command`-field prefix to a shape that works on every surface.

*   **Design decision**: Replace the four-line box with a `# Description: <text>\n___\n<command>` shape. The single-line prefix plus the `___` separator means: even on raw-JSON surfaces, the first readable token is still `# Description: <text>` followed by an underscore divider that's visually clear; on Markdown-rendering surfaces the `___` becomes a horizontal rule. The same text is mirrored to `updatedInput.description` (universal channel) and, for PowerShell, to `permissionDecisionReason` (the v1.1.0 visible-body channel for Claude Code's PowerShell dialog). Two `\n` characters total in the command-field prepend instead of four. Tokens saved roughly 10-20 per non-auto-approved shell call.

*   **Options considered and rejected**:
    *   **Surface-adaptive env detection** - no reliable cross-surface signal exists, and the matrix of (surface x platform x version) makes the maintenance burden too large.
    *   **Aggressive newline collapse on the command body** - breaks PowerShell here-strings (`@'...'@`) and Bash heredocs (`<<EOF`), which are exactly the multi-line commands users most want descriptions for (commit messages, file content).
    *   **Drop the in-command prefix entirely** - loses the in-transcript co-location of intent and command in chat history. Marginal benefit; the `description` field alone is enough for the live dialog but the inline `# Description:` line gives future LLM context a cleaner read.
    *   **Spill multi-line bodies to temp files** - aggressive UX change for low payoff; here-strings and heredocs are syntactically meaningful PowerShell / Bash constructs, not a wart to engineer around.

*   **Implementation**:
    *   **`catalog/hooks/format-bash-description.py`**: removed `_BOX_HEADER` / `_BOX_FOOTER` / `_MIN_CONTENT_WIDTH` / `_MAX_CONTENT_WIDTH` constants and the `format_description_box(text, *, width=None)` helper that used `textwrap.wrap`. Replaced with `_PREFIX_MAX_LEN = 120` and `format_description_prefix(text)` that collapses runs of whitespace (including newlines and tabs) into single spaces, trims, truncates at 120 chars with `...` ellipsis. Dropped `shutil` and `textwrap` imports. `main()` updated: `prefix + "\n" + cleaned_command` (single newline) instead of `box + "\n\n" + cleaned_command` (four newlines). Description-field value is normalized to single line via the same helper.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/format-powershell-description.py`**: mirror change. **Preserved verbatim** the v1.1.0 safety contract: `permissionDecision: "ask"` is still emitted on every non-allowed command, and `permissionDecisionReason` still carries the full normalized description (untruncated; only the inline prefix is truncated). Updated comment block explaining the design.
    *   **`format_description_box` alias**: kept in both hook files as a one-release-cycle compatibility shim for any external Python caller. Will be removed in the next minor release.
    *   **`strip_description_box`**: extended to drop leading underscore-only separator lines (the new `___` divider) in addition to the existing `#`-prefixed-line and blank-line strips. Absorbs every shape the hook has shipped: the legacy 4-line box, the intermediate `# desc:` prefix, and the current `# Description: <text>\n___\n<command>` shape. Regression tests cover all three shapes plus underscore-separator widths from 2 to 40 chars.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/require-description.sh` and `catalog/hooks/require-powershell-description.sh`**: agent-facing blurb examples updated to show the single-line `# Description: <text>` prefix. The fallback regex extended from `^[[:space:]]*#.*Description` to `^[[:space:]]*#.*\(desc:\|description\)` so a command starting with either the new prefix or the legacy box header satisfies the require-description check.
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-claude.md`**: replaced the two separate `MANDATORY` rules (one for Bash, one for PowerShell) with a single unified shell-tool rule covering Bash, PowerShell, `run_shell_command`, `shell`, etc. The Claude-specific footnote naming the four hooks (`format-bash-description.py`, `format-powershell-description.py`, `require-description.sh`, `require-powershell-description.sh`) is preserved at the end.
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-codex.md`** and **`templates/ai-instructions/base-gemini.md`**: replaced the Bash-only `MANDATORY` rule with the unified rule (no hook footnote - those platforms do not run the Claude hooks by name).
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-cursor.md`** and **`templates/ai-instructions/base-opencode.md`**: ADDED the unified rule into the `## Working Conventions` list. These two templates previously carried no Bash / PowerShell description guidance at all - this is new discipline for users on Cursor and OpenCode.
    *   **Tests**: `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_bash_description.py` and `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_powershell_description.py` rewrote `TestFormatDescriptionBox` -> `TestFormatDescriptionPrefix` with single-line shape assertions, empty-input placeholder, internal-whitespace collapse, and >120-char truncation. `TestStripDescriptionBox` updated to use the new prefix shape in round-trip tests; new `test_strips_legacy_box_format` regression guard ensures mid-conversation retries on legacy-formatted commands still strip cleanly. `TestMainIntegration` tests renamed and updated; in the PowerShell file, the load-bearing `permissionDecision == "ask"` and `permissionDecisionReason == "<description>"` assertions are preserved verbatim.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for the user beyond rerunning the installer. The new hooks land at the same paths and produce the same kind of approval-dialog output, just with a more compact and surface-portable prefix. Users on Cursor and OpenCode will see their agents start adding a `description` parameter to shell tool calls; this is the one new behavior that arrives with this change (those templates previously carried no rule).

*   **Verification**: 
    *   `make validate` clean (no `data/*.json` change).
    *   `make lint` clean (shell-script edits live inside quoted heredocs; no semantic change).
    *   `make test` green: `TestFormatDescriptionPrefix` (9 bash + 5 powershell), updated `TestStripDescriptionBox` (7 bash + 4 powershell including the new legacy-strip regression test), updated `TestMainIntegration`.
    *   Manual hook smoke: piped a synthetic payload with a 200-char description through both hooks; confirmed (a) `updatedInput.command` starts with `# Description: <truncated to 120 chars ending in ...>\n___\n`, (b) the body after the prefix and separator is byte-identical to the input command, (c) `updatedInput.command.count("\n") == 2 + original_command.count("\n")` (two newlines added: one after the prefix, one after the separator line), (d) for the PowerShell payload `permissionDecision == "ask"` and `permissionDecisionReason` carries the full untrimmed description.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: 
    *   The Claude Desktop app's raw-JSON rendering of the `command` field remains an upstream issue - this fix mitigates the symptom (description is always readable, prefix degrades gracefully) but does not eliminate it (a long multi-line `command` body still shows escaped `\n` characters in the Desktop dialog). The Desktop-app rendering bug is a separate workstream against `anthropics/claude-code`.
    *   The new "Cursor / OpenCode agents must provide a description" rule is added to those two platform templates for the first time. Agents on those platforms will start emitting descriptions on shell tool calls; if the agent forgets, the call still goes through (those platforms do not run the require-description hooks).

*   **Current Status**: ready for commit. Modified files: `catalog/hooks/format-bash-description.py`, `catalog/hooks/format-powershell-description.py`, `catalog/hooks/require-description.sh`, `catalog/hooks/require-powershell-description.sh`, `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_bash_description.py`, `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_powershell_description.py`, all five `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]`), `docs/DEVLOG.md` (this entry), plus the memory file `reference_powershell_dialog_rendering.md` appended with a Resolution subsection.

The plan ran as a single seven-phase content release per the user-supplied constraint that all phases ship together as v1.2.0; no intermediate version-string bumps anywhere across Phases 1-7.

*   **What shipped between v1.1.5 and v1.2.0**:
    *   **9 new skills** (catalog total 187 -> 196 user-facing skills): `doc-coauthoring` (Phase 2 / A9), `generative-art` / `theme-tokens` / `internal-comms` / `web-artifacts-builder` (Phase 4 / A1, A3, A8, A10), `skill-eval-loop` (Phase 5 / A6+A7), `brand-styling` / `mcp-builder` (Phase 6 / A2, A5).

All four registered explicitly in BOTH `scripts/installer.sh` AND `scripts/installer.ps1` per the AGENTS.md "Installer-Aware Changes" rule.

Documented in `AGENTS.md`, enforced by a new `--bundles-only` audit in `scripts/validate_skills.py`, wired into `make validate`, smoke-tested through both installer copy primitives.

    *   **One CLI-agnostic parity invariant** ported to a new file (Phase 5 / A7): `scripts/optimize_skill_description.py` carries the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent for claude / gemini / codex / opencode dispatch with no cross-CLI fallback, enforced by `catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py::TestEvalLoopCLIAdapter`.
    *   **One delivery channel opened** (Phase 7 / A16): the `.skill` ZIP archive format produced by `scripts/package_skill.py` lets users distribute DevAI-Hub-shaped skills to Claude.ai and the Anthropic API skill-upload endpoint.
    *   **36 new pytest cases** across three new modules: 8 in `test_skill_bundles.py` (Phase 3), 14 in `test_eval_loop.py` (Phase 5), 14 in `test_package_skill.py` (Phase 7). No removed tests.

*   **Wrap-up phase steps executed**:
    *   **Session history**: `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/development/history/2026-05-11_wrap-up-v1.2.0-release.md` (cumulative wrap-up summary alongside the seven per-phase histories).
    *   **`.gitignore`**: Added `*.skill` pattern (Phase 7 packager output is portable ZIP archives intended for upload, not for landing in the catalog tree). Other Phase 1-6 patterns (`*-workspace/` for eval-loop) were added in their respective phases.

    *   **Known-gaps sweep + finalize**: Re-read `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` end-to-end; the per-phase Append-mode runs were thorough, no new items surfaced in the wrap-up sweep. Finalized the file: `Status:` flipped to `finalized`, finalization note appended after the Summary table citing the v1.2.0 bump date. 11 open items remain in `## Open Items` for the next-version `/generate-plan` ingest step.
    *   **Memory**: Reviewed all entries; existing facts remain accurate. Added one new project memory capturing the cumulative cross-OS verification queue (DF-003 / DF-005 / DF-006 / DF-007 / DF-008) so the durable rule "run a real installer execution on Linux + macOS via CI matrix before tagging a MINOR / MAJOR release" survives into the next session.

Rationale: strictly additive features (9 new skills, 4 new scripts, new layout convention) with zero breaking changes and one cosmetic registry verification (Phase 2 / A4). Patch would understate the surface; major would overstate it because there is no removal or incompatible change. *   **Goal**: Execute Phase 6 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archive/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 6 ships two more skills consuming the Phase 3 / A13 layout convention: `brand-styling` (specialized-domains) - a token-pattern skill that applies user-supplied brand tokens (palette, typography, logo, voice) to generated artifacts via per-brand JSON files at `~/.devai-hub/brand/<slug>/tokens.json`, with EMPTY placeholders and zero vendor assets per the company-neutral framing rule (the user MUST supply their own brand) - and `mcp-builder` (ai-development) - a skill that walks the agent through building a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server in either Python (FastMCP) or Node / TypeScript (the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`), with bundled cross-platform scaffolding scripts for both stacks plus reference docs covering the deeper API surfaces. The mcp-builder skill enforces the AGENTS.md MCP Registry Policy decision tree before scaffolding (skill vs hook vs MCP triage) and documents settings.json registration across all five DevAI-Hub-supported AI CLIs. Phase 6 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **Implementation**:
    *   **A2 - `catalog/skills/specialized-domains/brand-styling/SKILL.md` (180 lines).** Token-pattern skill that extends the Phase 4 / A3 `theme-tokens` schema with brand-specific extensions: `logo` (primary / secondary / wordmark / `min_height_px` / `clear_space_factor`), `voice` (tone + do / dont rules), and `assets_dir` for self-hosted fonts / icons. Brands live entirely under `~/.devai-hub/brand/<slug>/{tokens.json, fonts/, logo.{svg,png}}`. Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14: verbatim trigger phrases ("our brand", "company colors", "brand guidelines", "brand kit", "house style", "match the brand", "use our typography", "apply our logo", "stay on-brand", "brand tokens", "brand consistency") plus an explicit `SKIP:` clause for brand-neutral artifacts (use theme-tokens), one-off styling, and vendor-specific brands the user does NOT own. Common Rationalizations table covers seven failure modes (the agent inventing "professional" colors, screenshot-as-brand-source, vendor-palette substitution, voice skipping, inline-only persistence, single-logo lock-in, silent defaults). The body is opinionated about TWO key behaviors: (1) ALWAYS ask the user for brand tokens before picking colors or fonts, and OFFER to scaffold an empty `~/.devai-hub/brand/default/tokens.json` if the user has none; (2) FAIL LOUDLY on missing required fields rather than silently substituting defaults. Bundled `templates/tokens.template.json` ships with all required keys present but every value empty / null / empty-string. Cross-links to `theme-tokens`, `pptx-generation`, `docx-generation`, `pdf-document-generation`, `web-artifacts-builder`, `internal-comms`, `writing-editing`, `technical-writer`. Verified via `git grep -i 'anthropic\|openai\|tailwind.*palette\|material.*color\|google.*brand'` against the skill folder - zero hits.
    *   **A5 - `catalog/skills/ai-development/mcp-builder/SKILL.md` (242 lines).** Skill that walks the agent through building a local MCP server in either Python (FastMCP) or Node / TypeScript (the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`), then registering the server across all five DevAI-Hub-supported AI CLIs. The skill is opinionated about Step 0: BEFORE scaffolding any server, walk the AGENTS.md MCP Registry Policy decision tree with the user. The "When to build vs. skill vs. hook" comparison table makes the triage concrete: skill when LLM-native, hook when one-shot lifecycle event, MCP when deterministic capability returning structured data the LLM cannot reliably do. Step 6 documents the settings.json registration shape across all five CLIs (Claude `~/.claude/settings.json`, Cursor `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, Codex `~/.codex/config.json`, Gemini `~/.gemini/mcp.json`, OpenCode `~/.config/opencode/mcp.json`); the entry shape is identical across all five. Common Rationalizations table covers eight common drift modes including search-as-service wrappers (categorically rejected by policy), MCP-when-skill-suffices, Step-0 skipping, HTTP-by-default, auth deferral, and terse tool descriptions (which under-trigger like skill descriptions do). Cross-links to `developer-experience/tool-design`, `workflow/create-skill-or-command`, `ai-development/ai-agent-development`, `ai-development/claude-agent-sdk`, `architecture/api-design`, `language-specialists/python-expert`, `language-specialists/typescript-expert`.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `references/` (2 files, both referenced from SKILL.md per the A13 audit).** `references/fastmcp.md` covers the deeper FastMCP API surface: install + minimum runtime, minimal server template, tool definitions with Pydantic models, transports (stdio default, HTTP, SSE), HTTP / SSE auth via FastAPI middleware, resources and prompts, four named testing patterns, six common pitfalls, and going-beyond-the-scaffold guidance. `references/ts-sdk.md` covers the same topics for Node / TypeScript with Zod schemas: install, minimal `McpServer` + `StdioServerTransport` template, tool definitions with `server.tool(name, schema, handler)` shape, transports, HTTP auth via Express middleware, resources and prompts, four testing patterns, six common pitfalls (especially ESM/CJS interop and `~` path-expansion bugs), and production-build guidance.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `scripts/` (4 files in two parallel pairs, all referenced from SKILL.md).** `scripts/init-mcp-fastmcp.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`) verifies Python 3.10+, creates `<name>/`, writes `pyproject.toml` with `mcp[cli]>=1.0.0` + `pydantic>=2.0.0` deps, writes `server.py` with one example `@mcp.tool()` decorated `echo` function returning a Pydantic `EchoResult` model, writes `.gitignore`, creates a venv at `.venv/`, installs the deps into the venv, prints next-step instructions including `mcp dev server.py`. `scripts/init-mcp-fastmcp.ps1` is the PowerShell sibling (same output, `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`). `scripts/init-mcp-ts.sh` verifies Node 20+, runs `npm init -y`, installs `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` + `zod` + `tsx` + `typescript` + `@types/node`, writes ESM-native `package.json` with `dev` / `build` / `start` scripts, writes `tsconfig.json` targeting ES2022 / ESNext / Bundler resolution, writes `src/server.ts` with one example `server.tool()` registration using a Zod schema and stdio transport, writes `.gitignore`, runs `npm install`, prints next-step instructions including `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector npm run dev`. `scripts/init-mcp-ts.ps1` is the PowerShell sibling. Summary table updated: 10 open items (was 9), 0 resolved this version. Last-updated date stamped 2026-05-08 (Phase 6 complete).

*   **Design Rationale**: Three calls shaped the Phase 6 work. **First**, the brand-styling skill's strongest opinion is that the agent must NOT invent brand decisions on the user's behalf. The pre-Phase-6 state of the world had no such guard - any artifact that needed a "brand-looking" treatment got one with the agent's defaults (typically the AI-slop palette: navy, gray, blue accent). The skill's body explicitly catches the rationalization "the user wants 'professional' colors - I'll just pick navy and gray" and rebuts it with: ASK the user for their brand; OFFER an empty default scaffold if they have none; FAIL LOUDLY if a required brand field is missing. The bundled template's empty placeholders make the contract concrete - the user CANNOT use the skill without filling values. The N1 dropped-outright item from the comparison report (Anthropic's actual brand colors / fonts / logo) drove this design: the skill captures the PATTERN without shipping any vendor assets, satisfying both the company-neutral framing rule (memory `feedback_no_employer_refs.md`) and the AGENTS.md reverse-engineering attribution rule. **Second**, the mcp-builder skill's most-load-bearing section is Step 0 (the policy-decision-tree walk), not the scaffolders themselves. Many requests for "an MCP that does X" are actually requests for "the agent to do X reliably", which is a SKILL not an MCP - the skill catches that case before any infrastructure is built. The "When to build vs. skill vs. hook" comparison table is the operational expression of Step 0. The four scaffolders (FastMCP bash + ps1, TS SDK bash + ps1) are intentionally minimal: each generates a one-tool hello-world `echo` server in under 30 seconds, deferring all production concerns (auth, multi-tool, distribution) to the reference docs. This matches the Phase 4 `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` precedent: the scaffolder's value is "30 seconds and no version-mismatch debugging", not "a complete production server". **Third**, the installer-edit decision was straightforward. The plan's prompt for sub-task 6.2 says "Register the four bundled scripts in BOTH installers per the AGENTS.md installer-aware changes rule." But AGENTS.md "Installer-Aware Changes" makes a clear distinction: per-skill bundled scripts under `catalog/skills/<>/scripts/` are auto-distributed via the recursive-copy logic (the `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` primitives validated in Phase 3 / WN-001), and only repo-level `scripts/<name>.py` artifacts require explicit-name registration. The Phase 4 web-artifacts-builder bundled `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` scripts were NOT registered explicitly - they ride the recursive copy. The Phase 6 mcp-builder scripts follow the same pattern. So no installer edit was made; verification was done via static analysis (bash -n + ShellCheck + PowerShell parse-check) and bundle-audit confirmation that all four scripts are referenced from the parent SKILL.md.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users beyond two new skills appearing in their installed catalog after the next installer run. No schema changes, no `settings.json` changes, no installer behavior changes (the recursive copy already handles bundled subdirs from Phase 3), no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up: (a) two new skill folders under `~/.claude/skills/specialized-domains/brand-styling/` and `~/.claude/skills/ai-development/mcp-builder/` (and the equivalent destinations for Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode) with their `templates/` and `references/` + `scripts/` subdirectories; (b) updated `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in each platform's `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`-rendered instruction file with the two new rows. **Important (carried forward through v1.1.5 phases 3-5)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skills to become callable. **For brand-styling**: users who want to apply their brand should populate `~/.devai-hub/brand/<their-brand-slug>/tokens.json` from the bundled `templates/tokens.template.json` BEFORE asking the agent to "stay on-brand"; the skill explicitly refuses to invent brand values on the user's behalf.

## [2026-05-08] - Phase 5 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: skill-eval-loop + description optimizer (A6, A7)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 5 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archive/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 5 ships the eval-iteration workflow + browser viewer + description optimizer as a single integrated skill, with a CLI-agnostic adapter following the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent (claude / gemini / codex / opencode parity). Specifically: (a) a new workflow skill `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/` that drives a closed-loop evaluation against any DevAI-Hub skill (paired with-skill / without-skill runs, assertion-graded outputs, browser-reviewed benchmarks, structured feedback capture, five named improvement heuristics); (b) three repo-level dispatcher scripts under `scripts/`: `aggregate_benchmark.py` (post-processes paired runs into `benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md`), `skill_eval_viewer.py` (server + static modes for browser-based eval review with feedback capture), `optimize_skill_description.py` (60/40 train-test split optimizer with held-out-test selection that prevents overfitting); (c) a parametrized pytest at `catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py` enforcing the no-cross-CLI-bleed invariant via source inspection (parametrized over four CLIs x one dispatcher = four parity assertions, plus dry-run schema and aggregator/viewer smoke). Phase 5 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A6.1 - `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/SKILL.md` (~200 lines).** Workflow skill with full DevAI-Hub frontmatter that drives the 10-step iteration loop. Steps 1-2 are one-time setup (capture user intent into `<workspace>/intent.md`; author 2-3 realistic test prompts to `evals/evals.json`). Steps 3-10 are the per-iteration loop: spawn paired `with_skill` / `without_skill` runs in `<workspace>/iteration-N/eval-XXX/{...}/outputs/`; capture `total_tokens` + `duration_ms` per run; grade against assertions via the bundled `agents/grader.md` sub-agent (exact field names `text` / `passed` / `evidence`); aggregate to `benchmark.json` via `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py`; launch `scripts/skill_eval_viewer.py`; collect `feedback.json` from the user's review; apply improvement heuristics from `references/improvement-heuristics.md`; re-run as `iteration-N+1`. Stop conditions documented: pass-rate stable across 2 consecutive iterations, OR explicit user accept, OR pass-rate regresses for 2 consecutive iterations (rolls back). Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14: trigger phrases include "evaluate a skill", "benchmark a skill", "A/B test a skill", "optimize a skill description", "run an eval set", "score a skill against test prompts", "iterate on a skill", "skill regression", "with-skill vs without-skill", "eval harness", "eval workspace", "paired runs", "eval iteration", "make this skill actually work"; `SKIP:` clause covers one-off prompt tests, ad-hoc skill drafting, deterministic-code unit tests, live-traffic A/B, and vendor-specific eval suites. Common Rationalizations table covers eight failure modes (eyeball-only, two-prompts-is-enough, tokens-don't-matter, held-out-test-is-overkill, manual-grading, with-skill-only, parity-test-is-bureaucracy, vibes-stop-condition). Verification checklist is binary and observable. Cross-links to `developer-experience/ai-output-evaluation`, `workflow/create-custom-command` + AGENTS.md, `tests-generation/code-coverage`, `orchestration/multi-agent-coordinator`, `developer-experience/prompt-engineering`, `workflow/known-gaps-tracker`.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `references/` (4 files, all linked from SKILL.md).** `schemas.md` documents the JSON schema for every artifact in the loop (`evals/evals.json`, per-run `run_metadata.json`, per-run `grading.json`, per-iteration `benchmark.json`, per-iteration `feedback.json`, per-optimizer-iteration result). `improvement-heuristics.md` documents the five heuristics applied at step 9 (H1 pushy descriptions, H2 explain-the-why, H3 repeated-work elimination, H4 negative-space coverage, H5 assertion calibration), each with symptom + fix + worked example + validation criterion, and the priority order (H1 -> H4 -> H2 -> H5 -> H3) with the one-heuristic-per-iteration constraint. `cli-adapter.md` documents the option-A-vs-option-B design rationale (option A = four parallel scripts, the v1.1.3 hooks pattern; option B = single dispatcher with `--cli` flag, selected for files of this size since duplication ratio 50:150 lines is too high to justify the deletion-safety affordance), the per-CLI invocation patterns for `claude` / `gemini` / `codex` / `opencode` (skill-loading flag + prompt flag + token-capture pattern per CLI), and the parity-test specification. `description-optimizer.md` documents the 60/40 train-test split rationale (without held-out, the optimizer picks descriptions that memorize train-query phrasing verbatim), the iteration structure (`<workspace>/optimizer/iteration-N.json` + `final.json`), the candidate-generation prompt template, the held-out-test selection rule (`max(pool, key=test_trigger_rate)` with train-rate + length tiebreakers, shorter wins to minimize Tier 1 token cost), and the `--dry-run` mode contract.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `agents/` (3 sub-agent prompt files).** `grader.md` instructs the grader sub-agent to evaluate assertions against a run's `outputs/response.txt` and write `grading.json` with the exact field names `text` / `passed` / `evidence` (the aggregator depends on these). The grader's six rules: read assertion text literally, evidence is mandatory and concrete (line number + quoted span), read response.txt cold without bias from prior turns, do not invent assertions, be conservative on borderline calls, no overall-quality opinions. `comparator.md` instructs the comparator sub-agent to perform a blind A/B comparison: the runner shuffles A/B per eval so the comparator never knows which is `with_skill`; verdict alphabet is exactly `A_better` / `B_better` / `tie`; six rules: read both cold, judge by query relevance not surface polish, use eval tags as context not scoring, cite concrete differences, default to `tie` when ambiguous, calibrate confidence honestly. `analyzer.md` instructs the analyzer sub-agent to read `benchmark.json` (and optionally the per-run `grading.json` files plus the previous iteration's `benchmark.json`) and surface three classes of finding: non-discriminating assertions (same `passed` value across `with_skill` AND `without_skill` for every eval -> recommend H5), high-variance evals (`stddev/mean > 0.3` -> recommend H3), time/token trade-offs (>2x ratio between with_skill and without_skill -> surface for owner decision). The analyzer caps recommendations at 3 per iteration and maps every recommendation to a heuristic in `references/improvement-heuristics.md`. The agent files sit under `agents/` (sibling to `references/`) - intentionally outside the A13 orphan-audit scope (`scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` only) since they are sub-agent prompts, not bundled scripts or assets.
    *   **A6.3 - `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py`.** Stdlib-only Python 3.10+ aggregator that walks `<workspace>/iteration-N/` and emits `benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md` in the same directory. Per-eval metrics: `pass_rate`, `duration_ms_mean`, `duration_ms_stddev`, `tokens_mean`, `tokens_stddev`, plus a `delta` block (`with_skill - without_skill` for each metric). Overall metrics: `with_skill_pass_rate`, `without_skill_pass_rate`, `pass_rate_delta`, `with_skill_duration_ms_mean`, `without_skill_duration_ms_mean`, `with_skill_tokens_mean`, `without_skill_tokens_mean`. Pure post-processing - no CLI invocation. Schema documented at `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/references/schemas.md`. `--output-dir` lets the user redirect output for non-destructive runs.
    *   **A6.3 - `scripts/skill_eval_viewer.py`.** Stdlib-only Python 3.10+ browser viewer with two modes. Server mode (default) starts an `http.server` on a random port, opens the user's browser via `webbrowser.open()` (suppressible via `--no-open`), and accepts `POST /submit-feedback` that writes `<iteration_dir>/feedback.json`. Static mode (`--static <path>`) writes a self-contained HTML file whose "Submit All Reviews" button downloads `feedback.json` as a JS Blob - designed for headless / CI environments. Two-tab UI: "Outputs" (per-eval, `with_skill` vs `without_skill` side-by-side, with assertion-grading badges color-coded green/red, run-metadata badges showing duration / tokens / cli, free-form feedback textareas + a 3-option verdict selector per eval) and "Benchmark" (the `benchmark.json` table). Templating done with `str.format` - no jinja dependency.
    *   **A7 - `scripts/optimize_skill_description.py`.** Description optimizer with deterministic 60/40 train-test split (`--seed` default 42; `--train-fraction` configurable). For each iteration: `estimate_trigger_rate()` runs each train query `--repeats` times (default 3) under the current description and computes the per-query trigger rate; `generate_candidates()` asks the chosen CLI to PROPOSE 3 candidate description rewrites via the prompt template at `references/description-optimizer.md`; each candidate is evaluated on train AND test; `select_best()` picks the candidate with the highest `test_trigger_rate`, ties broken by `train_trigger_rate` then by description length (shorter wins per the AGENTS.md three-tier loading model where Tier 1 fields cost tokens on every catalog read). The optimizer terminates when `--max-iterations` (default 5) is reached, OR two consecutive iterations show no improvement in `test_trigger_rate` (early-stop), OR `test_trigger_rate` reaches 1.0. The `--dry-run` mode prints the train/test split, the baseline description, and the candidate-generation prompt template, then exits 0 without invoking any CLI - the pytest at `test_eval_loop.py::TestOptimizerDryRun` verifies this contract under three sub-cases (schema, determinism under fixed seed, no-CLI-invocation under empty PATH). CLI dispatch follows the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent: `assert cli in {"claude", "gemini", "codex", "opencode"}` near the top of `invoke_cli()`, four parallel `if cli == "X":` branches, no cross-CLI fallback. The parity invariant is enforced by `test_eval_loop.py::TestEvalLoopCLIAdapter`.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py` (14 tests, all green).** Three test classes: (1) `TestEvalLoopCLIAdapter` - parametrized over (`optimize_skill_description.py`, each of the four supported CLIs) plus `test_dispatcher_has_assertion_against_unsupported_cli` and `test_dispatcher_has_branch_for_each_cli`; the source-inspection technique mirrors `test_diff_review_hooks.py::TestPlatformIndependence` (find the `if cli == "X":` line, walk forward collecting lines whose indent is strictly greater than the header's indent, stop at the next sibling line, then assert no other CLI binary appears in argv-list form within the collected body). (2) `TestOptimizerDryRun` - asserts `--dry-run` returns 0 with the declared schema (`mode` / `cli` / `selection_metric` / `n_train` / `n_test` / `split` / `baseline_description` / `candidate_generation_prompt_template_preview`), the split is deterministic for the same `--seed`, and the optimizer does NOT invoke any CLI when run with `PATH` pointing at an empty directory (the strongest evidence of dry-run isolation). (3) `TestAggregator` and `TestViewerStaticMode` - build a fixture iteration directory with one eval, paired runs, and `grading.json`, run the aggregator, assert `benchmark.json` has `with_skill_pass_rate=1.0` / `without_skill_pass_rate=0.0` / `pass_rate_delta=1.0`, then run the viewer with `--static review.html` and assert the HTML body contains the eval id, both run-condition labels, and the `submitFeedback` JS function name (proves the viewer renders the static-mode submit handler).
    *   **Both installers updated in lockstep.** `scripts/installer.sh` gains a Phase-5 `safe_copy` block (line ~1424) that registers `aggregate_benchmark.py` + `skill_eval_viewer.py` + `optimize_skill_description.py` to `~/.devai-hub/scripts/`, modeled after the existing `generate_report.py` / `devai_mcp_benchmark.py` blocks. `scripts/installer.ps1` gains the matching PowerShell `Safe-Copy` block (line ~1735) using `Join-Path $RepoRoot "scripts\<name>.py"` and `Join-Path $scriptsDest "<name>.py"`. Both blocks include the same comment header explaining why these are repo-level scripts that need explicit registration (vs the per-skill bundled scripts under `catalog/skills/.../scripts/` which are auto-distributed by the recursive copy).
    *   **Registry updates.** `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gets one new `skill-eval-loop` row in the workflow category; total 191 -> 192. `data/skills.json` gets one new entry (full schema, version=1.0.0, category=workflow, language=Python, tags=[skill-evaluation, ab-testing, benchmark, eval-harness, paired-runs, iteration-loop, description-optimizer, cli-agnostic, held-out-test], priority=MEDIUM, tools_required=[Read, Write, Edit, Bash], status=production, security 100/100/95); `statistics.total_skills` 193 -> 194; `statistics.categories.workflow` 18 -> 19. `data/marketplace.json` workflow category description updated to mention "skill evaluation"; `skill_count` 19 -> 20.
    *   **`.gitignore` updated.** New `*-workspace/` entry to ignore user-generated eval workspaces. The loop creates `<skill-name>-workspace/` directories at the repo root with per-iteration outputs, benchmarks, and feedback that should not leak into commits.

*   **Design Rationale**: The first key call was **option A vs option B for the CLI adapter**. Option A (four parallel scripts) is the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent applied verbatim. Option B (single dispatcher with `--cli` flag) was selected because the eval-loop dispatchers are 250-400 lines each; replicating ~150 lines of workspace-layout / JSON-I/O / paired-run plumbing across four scripts produces 600 lines of duplication for ~50 lines of CLI-specific logic per script. The v1.1.3 hooks were 80 lines each, so duplication was acceptable; it is not at this size. Option B preserves the parity invariant via a 50-line pytest module that source-inspects each `if cli == "X":` branch, which is a much lower maintenance cost than four parallel files. The second call was **whether to make the orphan-bundle audit fail-closed on `agents/`**. The validator's `BUNDLED_SUBDIRS` constant covers `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` only; sub-agent prompt files live under `agents/`, which is outside the audit scope. The plan prompt for sub-task 5.5 specifies `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/agents/`, and the AGENTS.md "Per-skill Bundled Resources" section says `MAY (not MUST) contain three subdirectories` and explicitly does not forbid other names. So `agents/` is auto-distributed by the recursive `safe_folder_copy` like every other subdirectory in the skill folder, but is not subject to the orphan audit. The third call was **selection metric for the optimizer**. The plan called for `best_description` selection by held-out test score; the alternative was train score plus regularization. Held-out test was selected because the candidate-generation prompt SEES the train queries (via the "queries that the description CURRENTLY MISHANDLES" block) and would therefore tune candidates to those specific phrasings; the held-out test set is the only signal that measures generalization. Tie-breakers added: train-rate (more general descriptions among equally-effective candidates) and description length (shorter wins, since description is Tier 1 metadata loaded on every catalog read). Length-as-tiebreaker is what the AGENTS.md three-tier loading model rationalizes - 50 saved tokens times the number of catalog reads per session adds up.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users beyond the new skill appearing in their installed catalog and three new repo-level scripts being available at `~/.devai-hub/scripts/{aggregate_benchmark,skill_eval_viewer,optimize_skill_description}.py` after the next installer run. No schema changes, no `settings.json` changes, no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up: (a) one new skill folder at `~/.claude/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/` (and the equivalent destinations for Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode) with the full `references/` + `agents/` subdirectories; (b) three new scripts under `~/.devai-hub/scripts/`; (c) updated `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in each platform's `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`-rendered instruction file with the new row. **Important (carried from v1.1.4 / v1.1.5 Phases 3-4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skill to become callable.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: Two new items in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`: DF-006 (Phase 5 cross-OS installer dry-run deferred - extends DF-003 / DF-005 with the Phase-5-specific context that the three new scripts need real `bash scripts/installer.sh` execution on a real macOS / Linux host before the v1.1.5 -> v1.2.0 version bump) and MT-001 (the optimizer's `run_iteration()` function lacks a "stub CLI binary on PATH" smoke test analogous to the v1.1.3 hooks - covered indirectly via the parity test + dry-run schema test, but a direct integration test would be stronger; out of scope for v1.1.5 if Phase 7 ships first). Carried over from earlier phases: DF-001, DF-002, DF-003, DF-004, DF-005, QG-001, WN-001. Total open: 9. Phase 6 starts next; it ships `brand-styling` (specialized-domains, token-pattern only - no vendor assets) and `mcp-builder` (ai-development, FastMCP + TS SDK runbook with bundled scaffolding scripts). Both Phase 6 skills will exercise the same `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` recursive-copy primitives this Phase 5 work confirmed clean.

*   **Test Posture**: All four test suites green. `python -c "json.load(...)"` passes for `data/skills.json` (194 skills, +1 from Phase 4 close), `data/bundles.json`, `data/marketplace.json`, `data/workflows.json`, `data/templates.json`. `python -m pytest catalog/hooks/tests/` results: **332 passed, 0 failures** (+14 new from `test_eval_loop.py` on top of the +8 from Phase 3 / `test_skill_bundles.py`). Total **428 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures**. `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` against the 198-skill catalog: **0 errors, 4 warnings** (carried from WN-001; no new orphans introduced).
